I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release.
  • Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found.
  • Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is right now expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

In a recent development, this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some vital ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

One thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

Industry observers note that it’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few.

It’s been a very long time since Canonical had a disappointing release, and 27.04 will keep up that trend.

The release schedule for Ubuntu 27.04 looks like this:.

To find out more, check out the official Ubuntu 27.04 release notes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that today is likely to be a historic one for the stock market.
  • AI stocks have been driving market direction over the past few years amid investors' enthusiasm about this new opportunity in tech.
  • Industry observers note that now, Anthropic is the first AI lab to go public, offering investors a fresh AI investing opportunity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adria Cimino – Nov 19, 2026 at 6:05AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

It has been revealed that today is likely to be a historic one for the stock market. Anthropic (ANT +0.00%), one of the most well-known names in artificial intelligence (AI), is making its market debut. The AI lab priced its initial public offering at $83 yesterday, increased its offering due to high demand, and raised more than $81 billion in the biggest IPO on record. This surpasses Space Exploration Technologies, which held the record until this point.

AI stocks have been driving market direction over the past few years amid investors' enthusiasm about this new opportunity in tech. This "next big thing" could make companies more efficient and innovative, and therefore power earnings higher. Chip designers and manufacturers, as well as cloud services companies, have been big winners in this movement so far.

Industry observers note that now, Anthropic is the first AI lab to go public, offering investors a fresh AI investing opportunity. (Rival OpenAI claims it aims to launch an IPO at some point but hasn't offered a time frame.).

Here's what to watch when Anthropic starts trading.

Industry observers note that so first, a quick catch-up on Anthropic and its IPO. The firm, founded by Dario Amodei and a small group of researchers -- all formerly of OpenAI -- back in 2021, is the name behind AI model Claude. The various versions of this model have helped Anthropic's revenue soar over the past three years as individuals and enterprise customers rush to use it. For example, in the first nine months of this year, revenue soared more than 1,200% to about $33 billion.

Sources indicate that anthropic increased the number of shares sold to 980 million and priced them at $83 apiece, raising $81.3 billion. SpaceX, by comparison, raised $75 billion during its IPO, then through the exercise of an overallotment option, that figure increased to more than $85 billion.

Now, let's consider what to watch today as Anthropic trading begins. It's important to note that IPO stocks generally start trading well after the 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time market opening. This is because market makers and underwriters must hold an auction to determine an opening price. Buy and sell orders will come in and be collected, and the official opening will take place when a price is established and a certain equilibrium among orders is in place -- so that normal trading can unfold for the rest of the trading day. It's possible that Anthropic shares will begin trading late in the morning or around noon.

According to recent reports, the company will debut with a fully diluted -- this accounts for all shares that exist -- market value of about $1.5 trillion, putting it on par with today's market giants such as Nvidia and Apple. It took years of trading for these older tech powerhouses to reach a trillion-dollar market cap, so Anthropic's entry at this level illustrates the magnitude of the AI investing theme.

Sources indicate that this year, other AI-related IPO stocks rose on their first day of trading, with Cerebras Systems climbing 68% and SpaceX advancing almost 20%. So, if history is a guide, today could be a positive one for Anthropic and its shareholders. And this means that companies that have invested in Anthropic, such as Amazon and Alphabet, also may see positive momentum today.

Industry observers note that amid all of the excitement, however, it's vital to remember that one or even a few days of trading won't determine whether the organization or the investor is successful over the long term. If you're thinking of investing in Anthropic, it's critical to consider the full picture, including the potential risks and rewards. And if you decide it's right for you, aim to buy at a reasonable price -- this might mean waiting for a dip -- and hold for the long term.

Breaking: Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that ford’s latest LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection.
  • Sources indicate that conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish.
  • So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ford’s latest LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection. During my visit this week to the automaker’s newly operational battery plant, engineers proudly showed me a video of the battery being crash-tested, the shell and the prismatic cells within bending violently under the force. My jaw practically hit the floor.

Sources indicate that conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish. Years of lithium-ion batteries in phones, tablets and laptops taught us that and it’s largely held true for electric cars as well.

So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.

Sources indicate that ford dropped that bombshell of a video on me at the end of my tour of its Blue Oval Battery Park outside Marshall, Michigan. However, I was barred from recording or photographing the footage.

It has been revealed that the design team’s mantra was “don’t assume a cell must never deform.” For the upcoming Fathom and Ford’s Universal EV platform, or UEV, the pack is designed to carry up to 40% of side-impact forces and is treated as part of the vehicle’s crash structure. The company’s leadership and engineers are confident that the EV won’t catch fire or explode despite the bent cells.

“Traditionally the battery is thought of as payload, a fragile jewel you must protect,” said Vladimir Bogachuk, chief engineer for advanced vehicle structure architecture at Ford. That approach, he said, means heavy bracing and protective structures around the pack. “The battery is not a jewel you must protect,” he said.

According to recent reports, bogachuk (along with every other Ford engineer and executive I spoke with that day) takes a less-is-more stance on the new EV platform. “The best part is no part,” he told me, “and if you have to have a part, it’s pretty much got to serve multiple functions.” And so the engineers set out to remove unnecessary armor and build a battery that serves double duty as an energy reservoir and crash structure.

Without that extra protection, the resulting EV can be lighter and more efficient, with improved driving dynamics. The UEV pack is deeply integrated into the vehicle’s structure: Its top lid is the cabin floor, and the seats bolt directly onto it. The bottom of the pack is the EV’s underbody. A service door beneath the Fathom’s rear seats will provide access to the charging and power electronics for service without the need to drop the pack.

Recent findings suggest that the crash videos showed deformation that would scare me on an older EV, but when I stopped to think, it wasn’t much different from what I’ve seen in conventional car side-impact crash tests. Ford notes an impact strong enough to deform the battery would also deform the chassis of a conventional vehicle or traditional EV, so the vehicle would likely be totaled anyway. More importantly, the engineers say the driver would be safe from thermal runaway and fire.

According to recent reports, when asked, Ford’s engineers noted they don’t believe in a “right chemistry” for every electric vehicle. The UEV platform’s LFP — short for lithium iron phosphate — chemistry, prismatic cells and “jelly roll” construction were chosen for low manufacturing cost, resistance to temperature extremes, suitability for bidirectional energy use and the ability to deform while remaining inert under designed loads and forces.

Other automakers have floated solid-state batteries as a potential solution to battery safety and energy density, but the technology isn’t ready for use in production cars — at least not at the scale and price that Ford needs for the reasonably priced Fathom.

According to recent reports, ford hasn’t stated the LFP pack’s energy capacity, the cell capacity or the number of cells the Fathom’s pack will comprise. Based on a cutaway displayed during my tour, I estimate 90 to 108 individual prismatic cells. The aluminum prismatic cans that enclose the cathode-anode “jelly roll” battery provide structural support and aid thermal dissipation throughout the larger pack.

Recent findings suggest that wes Thibault, chief engineer for global energy storage systems, described the rigorous validation that the cells and packs underwent to reach the point where they can be trusted to bend like a taco. He told me that Ford has “a dedicated abuse-testing team” integrated with battery design and engineering at every level and stage of the manufacturing process, searching for edge cases and probing the limits of what the chemistry, the cells and full production-spec battery packs can take, from withstanding over 150,000 miles of simulated daily driving to remaining safe and inert in a crash. Along the way, CT scans of the cells offered an inside look at the jelly roll and how it was responding.

Ford’s testing covers structural integrity and load-bearing capability, heat soak from minus 40 to 60 degrees Celsius, IP67 water resistance and humidity cycling, and high-charge and high-discharge tests. For multiaxis vibration, the battery, seats and brackets are strapped to what I can describe only as a giant mechanical bull that shakes the hardware through roll, pitch, yaw and multiple harmonic frequencies. Ford can combine multiple factors in a single test, such as a high-humidity heat soak under vibration during high discharge.

Once the first batch of UEV vehicles are on the road, Ford says it’ll be able to capture real-world data from the fleet to further fine-tune its validation methods for future generations of EVs.

Given how well the first model year of Ford’s Mustang Mach-E‘s batteries have held up after six years and thousands of real-world miles, it’s clear the automaker knows a thing or two about building a reliable battery.

It has been revealed that that said, the UEV platform’s LFP chemistry and construction are very different from those of the earlier generation, and the automaker is asking much, much more of the pack than just holding and discharging energy. It’s asking the pack to actively protect the souls onboard in the event of a crash. Testing to failure early and learning from those mistakes promptly is something the engineers I spoke to seem to take very seriously.

This bold, out-of-the-box approach to how the automaker thinks about battery fragility — protecting the souls onboard rather than the “jewel” that is the battery from a potential crash at the end of the vehicle’s life — comes with the promise of more range and efficiency, less weight and more driving fun over the vehicle’s lifetime.

Sources indicate that I’m ready to believe. I want EV batteries to be safer and less scary. That promise depends heavily on whether the Fathom’s UEV battery pack is as safe as Ford claims it is when it reaches driveways and dealerships in late 2027.

Industry observers note that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Ford. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving update. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

In a recent development, the v26.45 enhancement concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch consumers can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s newly introduced model worth it?

Industry observers note that constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how rapidly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The upgrade improves battery life without consumers having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

Sources indicate that that’s not the only Google Play Services enhancement that Wear OS smartwatch consumers can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been a wild week for the AI industry — and it’s only Thursday. Aside from outages, cheating scandals and Anthropic’s pending IPO, there are several latest models available now. Microsoft dropped seven new versions of its MAI models at its Ignite conference, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, the next step forward for its flagship models.

First, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

It’s clear from Microsoft’s marketing that it is aiming to position its new tech as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s leading models, with many of these significantly cheaper to run at the enterprise level. That, plus its new licensed weight program, which lets companies customize the new AI models for their purposes, highlights how Microsoft is continuing to pitch its AI tech to the workplace.

Industry observers note that while these newly introduced models might be useful for AI power customers, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the firm rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

And let’s not forget about Anthropic. The Claude maker prepares to become a public firm this week, with the possible biggest-ever IPO slated for Thursday. Anthropic is reportedly seeking an opening price of $83 per share, valuing it at $1.5 trillion — narrowly surpassing the valuation of Elon Musk’s mega-conglomerate, SpaceX, at its record-setting IPO earlier this year (now with SpaceXSI, because President Donald Trump remarked so).

According to recent reports, the Nvidia scandal caused a drastic 14% dip in its stock price during its first week and wiped out $1 trillion in the firm’s value, but Anthropic investors don’t seem to be worried. At least, not publicly.

Sources indicate that if nothing else, Anthropic’s IPO and the new models from OpenAI and Microsoft are stark reminders that the tech industry is nowhere near ready to slow down on AI. Even as financial, environmental and legal concerns mount — and arguably hit a fever pitch during the midterm elections — Major Tech is plowing ahead with generative AI.

  • Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

In a recent development, salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Recent findings suggest that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

According to recent reports, shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent consumers using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Industry observers note that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

Recent findings suggest that need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected].

Jumia (JMIA -11.13%) reported a narrowing of its quarterly loss and double-digit revenue growth while simultaneously lowering its full-year guidance due to deteriorating conditions in key markets. Management reported that while business fundamentals remain stable, external factors including smartphone supply shortages and a collapse in cocoa farmgate prices have constrained consumer purchasing power. The tech giant completed a $50 million capital raise during the quarter, anchored by the International Finance Corporation, to strengthen its balance sheet and provide flexibility for growth initiatives in 2027. Despite current headwinds, management confirmed its expectation to achieve positive cash flow in the fourth quarter of 2026 by selling through inventory and collecting corporate receivables.

#39149. World of Hyatt Adds Milestone Rewards, New Delta Benefits

World of Hyatt Adds Milestone Rewards, New Delta Benefits

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1156 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s going to be easier to rack up extra benefits if you’re a frequent Hyatt customer in 2027.
  • In a recent development, the news expands on the fresh details revealed Nov.
  • The additions to the Milestone Rewards are designed to give members more choice and personalization, according to Laurie Blair, senior vice president of global marketing and loyalty at Hyatt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s going to be easier to rack up extra benefits if you’re a frequent Hyatt customer in 2027. World of Hyatt revealed new Milestone Rewards, the ability to stack awards (such as Free Night Certificates and Suite Upgrade Awards) on a single stay and a simpler 365-day expiration on all awards.

In a recent development, the news expands on the fresh details revealed Nov. 17, 2026, around World of Hyatt’s partnership with Delta SkyMiles, which was first unveiled in September.

The additions to the Milestone Rewards are designed to give members more choice and personalization, according to Laurie Blair, senior vice president of global marketing and loyalty at Hyatt.

"We’re shaping the future of World of Hyatt around what our members value most. After a year of listening, one thing is clear: members want more distinctive benefits, more freedom to use their awards and the opportunity to choose awards that matter most to them,” Blair stated in an email to NerdWallet.

But top-tier Globalist members will soon have to choose between perks that they previously received automatically. Most notably, Globalists will no longer receive free parking on award nights in 2027. Instead, they can choose a Free Parking Award as a Milestone Reward that they can apply to award or paid stays.

The Delta Air Lines and Hyatt partnership will also mainly benefit frequent flyers and hotel guests. With the exception of the limited-time intro promotion, only Delta or Hyatt members with elite status will earn points in both programs. Hyatt elites will have to purchase premium tickets on Delta — not economy — to earn Hyatt points on the flight.

Here’s a breakdown of what’s changing:.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, World of Hyatt will extend Milestone Rewards to guests who have not yet qualified for the first level of elite status. Southwest Airlines did the same in its recent revamp to give loyal customers a thank you before they’ve reached any level of elite status.

In a recent development, world of Hyatt members will reach the first Milestone Reward at just 10 nights or 20,000 Base Points. Previously, it was 20 nights or 35,000 Base Points.

The reward choices at the first milestone are:.

A tier-qualifying night credit, which gets you closer to the next level of elite status.

A $25 FIND Experience credit (Hyatt’s platform for local experiences such as cooking classes).

A $30 spa credit good at Hyatt Inclusive Collection resorts.

The latter two will likely still require you to pay money out of pocket to use them, as the credit will only cover a portion of your bill. For example, the cheapest spa treatment at Secrets Playa Mujeres Golf & Spa Resort in Cancun, Mexico, will still run you $109 (or $79 after the credit).

The Milestone Rewards start to get good at the higher tiers. Starting at 20 nights, you can select from the existing Milestone Rewards, as well as new items. Some of the new options include:.

A Delta Air Lines eCertificate.

Free parking on award nights is going away as a Globalist tier benefit. In 2027, a Free Parking Award will be an option that Globalists can select at the 60, 70, 80 and 90 nights The parking award can be used on either a qualifying award or paid stay for up to seven nights.

Hyatt noted in a call with NerdWallet that roughly 70% of Globalists weren’t using the free parking benefit at all.

Globalists who have earned status in 2026 for 2027 will be grandfathered into the automatic free parking on award stays through their tier expiration date in February 2028.

To use these new awards, the Hyatt booking process is also getting an upgrade. Previously, awards like Suite Upgrade Awards and Free Night Awards couldn’t be redeemed on the same stay. Starting in 2027, members can combine eligible awards on a single reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and Free Parking Awards.

The new booking system will also make it easier to pay for some nights of a single reservation with awards, points, cash or a combination of points and cash.

Recent findings suggest that every award earned going forward will also carry a 365-day expiration from the date it’s issued, replacing the patchwork of different validity windows. Previously, Suite Upgrade and Guest of Honor Awards expired at “rest of year plus 14 days,” which was just a tad confusing. Meanwhile, Free Night Awards earned through Milestone Rewards were valid for 180 days from the date of issuance, which was not a lot of time to strategy a trip.

The Milestone Rewards kick in next year, but the other massive change around the Delta partnership is available now.

Hyatt elite members can earn World of Hyatt Bonus Points on eligible Delta flights (Delta Comfort, Premium Select, First Class and Delta One). Basic Economy or standard Main Cabin fares will earn nothing from this partnership at all.

Discoverist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $2 spent.

Explorist, Globalist and Lifetime Globalist members earn 1 Bonus Point per $1 spent.

Delta Medallion members (Silver through Diamond) can earn 1 Delta mile per $1 spent at participating Hyatt properties, on top of their regular Hyatt points.

Even if you don’t have elite status with either program, it’s still worth linking accounts to take advantage of the upcoming bonus point promotions:.

Those who link their accounts and complete a qualifying Hyatt stay from Nov. 17 to Dec. 31, 2026, will earn one bonus Tier-Qualifying Night Credit.

A second bonus point offer runs Jan. 4 through Feb. 15, 2027, for members who take their first Delta flight or Hyatt stay after linking their accounts. Members will earn 1,000 Delta SkyMiles after the Hyatt stay or 1,000 Hyatt points after their first flight in a premium cabin on Delta.

In a recent development, hyatt and Delta are also holding a sweepstakes through Nov. 23 — no points or miles required to enter — for a free three-night trip for two at Alila Mayakoba in Riviera Maya, Mexico, plus two $1,000 Delta gift cards. Linking your accounts before entering gets you a bonus entry.

If you are interested in dual accrual in 2027, there are some routes to elite status through travel credit cards. Hyatt’s entry-level elite tier comes as a benefit of holding the World of Hyatt Credit Card, but Discoverists earn Hyatt points at half the rate of Explorist and Globalist elites on premium Delta fares.

You want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s key to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
  • Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.
  • OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

Recent findings suggest that if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The firm already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Industry observers note that gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro blueprint, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Recent findings suggest that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US customers can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The latest landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Recent findings suggest that “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets owners view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

  • Apple says the revision provides bug fixes and security updates for complications on your iPhone, two of which may lead to memory corruption on your device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on Monday, Nov. 9, the same day the manufacturer released the first public beta for the upcoming iOS 27.3. The latest iPhone update fixes nine issues on your device, including a couple that could expose your data to malicious actors.

You can download iOS 27.2.1 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

Apple says the revision provides bug fixes and security updates for complications on your iPhone, two of which may lead to memory corruption on your device.

Memory corruption happens when a program on your device incorrectly reads, writes or frees up memory. This can cause the program to crash, or it could expose sensitive data to others.

It has been revealed that you should patch your iPhone as soon as possible. Apple didn’t say that these complications were being actively exploited. However, it’s vital to keep the software on your device up to date so you’re better protected against potential security threats.

  • Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a new and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful fresh features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

Industry observers note that first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

Sources indicate that A newly introduced feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a fresh feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

In a recent development, the new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

In a recent development, normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the newly introduced Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Some of the newly introduced features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’s a great day for designers who hate AI.
  • Recent findings suggest that the settings are available now for free and paying people globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia.
  • It has been revealed that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s a great day for designers who hate AI. Canva, the online design and publishing platform, revealed on Thursday that it’s introducing two fresh settings to opt out of seeing and using AI tools. One lets you turn off AI tools in Canva, and the other lets you filter out AI-created content from Canva’s library of templates and other elements.

Recent findings suggest that the settings are available now for free and paying people globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia. Canva administrators for business and team prepares can enable the two new settings for their entire organization.

It has been revealed that to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off. To filter out AI in your Canva library, go to Profile > Your account > AI personalization and enable the feature that notes show less AI-generated content.

Sources indicate that it’s hard not to compare Canva’s new opt-out features to Adobe, which spent all of last week at Adobe Max trying to convince creative professionals to embrace its AI tools. Adobe’s chief technology officer told CNET that he thought the problem was slop, not AI.

According to recent reports, as criticisms of AI mount, it’s smart, albeit rare, to see a tech manufacturer give its users a definitive, one-click solution to filter out AI tools. We will have to put Canva’s settings to the test to see how effectively they work, though.

Sources indicate that if you do want to use AI, Canva has no shortage. Its magic layers tool lets you break apart an AI-generated image into editable layers, a hugely helpful capability for fixing errors and customizing content. Its foundational models, along with other third-party models, can help you generate new image, video and audio content. Outside of graphic design, Canva has added AI tools for spreadsheet, document and presentation work over the past year. And like every other tech company, Canva claims it aims to continue investing in AI.

For more, check out our guides to muting Meta AI and disabling Google’s AI on your Pixel.

Industry News: Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • According to recent reports, the upcoming Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the upcoming Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

According to recent reports, the upcoming Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app consumers on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the latest Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

It has been revealed that one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

#39135. iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1972 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review.
  • Industry observers note that apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done.
  • Still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review. Well, mostly.

Industry observers note that apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done. I’ve grown so accustomed to using it that I sometimes forget how much attention it draws when I pull it out of my pocket, especially given its limited availability and lengthy preorder windows – not to mention its sky-high $1,999 starting price.

Still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design. The Duo’s cameras pull their weight with casual photography, but while filming social content at F1’s US Grand Prix and chatting with filmmakers at an SFFilm screening, I couldn’t resist going for the best cameras at my disposal on the Pro Max. There are times a conventional slab phone just does the trick – without all the frills and novelty of a folding one.

Recent findings suggest that that hasn’t stopped me from keeping the Duo as my primary device. It’s an enjoyable phone to use, with its compact, palm-sized build and spacious inner display. Plus, as CNET’s ongoing folding test demonstrates, it has a durable build that ensures I can fold and unfold it to my heart’s content.

And if I’m being honest, I kind of love how much of a statement piece it’s become.

In a recent development, the Duo’s versatility has really shown its appeal the more I live with it. I find myself using the 5.4-inch cover screen and 7.6-inch inner display pretty equally, demonstrating the practicality of each.

Recent findings suggest that when I’m on the move, the cover screen suffices for sending texts, responding to emails and checking notifications. Lounging around at home, I’m more inclined to use the larger inner display to endlessly scroll through Instagram or binge YouTube videos.

Sources indicate that the matte inner display remains one of my favorite elements. It reduces the appearance of the crease as well as glare, making it easier to see content even outdoors. Yes, the coating can dim the vibrant colors in images and videos, even with the screen’s 3,000-nit peak brightness, and smudges become prominent. But I can live with both of those drawbacks, and a microfiber cloth fixes the latter.

Apple’s phone-tablet hybrid came in clutch when I was on a recent flight and didn’t want to pull out my laptop. Instead, I used the Duo’s split-screen mode to place the Notes app on one half of the screen and an informational video on the other so I could rapidly jot down the main points. The Duo has also become my gym buddy; I prop it open on the treadmill so I can watch Magpie Murders on a tablet-like display, then fold it up and toss it in my pocket when I’m done.

In a recent development, apple Pencil support really helps the Duo feel like a mini iPad, and the matte coating on the inner display adds a satisfying resistance that more closely emulates the feel of writing on paper than a glossy surface. It gives jotting down notes, highlighting book passages and marking up documents a more tactile feel. I’m not much of a doodler, but I imagine that’s fun, too.

Sources indicate that the Apple Pencil can magnetically attach to the outer surface of the hinge, though it definitely sticks out, so there’s not really a practical, secure way to carry it around with the Duo (at least not that Apple has shared, but case-makers are sure to cook up a solution). I’m glad the stylus also works on the Duo’s cover screen, though the smaller size and glossy display make that experience slightly less satisfying.

Industry observers note that the number of apps optimized for the Duo at launch was relatively small, but it’s steadily increased. I gasped aloud on the train platform one morning while sending an email, realizing Gmail had finally been adapted for the Duo. It’s refreshing to see apps that feel intentional and fill the screen, rather than being awkwardly letterboxed.

It has been revealed that apple mentioned in early November that more than 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo were live in the App Store. A week later, that number ballooned to over 200,000 apps. So despite a rather slow start, virtually all apps I regularly use now work seamlessly on Apple’s foldable.

One of my favorite apps on the Duo is Instagram’s Edits. When holding the phone open in landscape orientation, I can view the video timeline and make edits on the right side of the screen while seeing a preview of the video on the left. Rotated to portrait orientation, the layout resembles the interface on a traditional smartphone, but on a larger scale, which is helpful especially for making smaller tweaks.

It’s great to see more apps that don’t just expand to the larger screen, but make meaningful use of the Duo’s design.

As I found during my review, the Duo’s battery life has been pretty good. It consistently lasts through the day, even as I hop between displays. I usually charge my phone at night, but even if I don’t, I know I’ll have some remaining battery in the morning.

Sources indicate that for instance, one day I started at 6:30 a.m. with a full battery. After my usual routine of checking emails, texting, scrolling through social media and browsing YouTube throughout the day, my battery was at 55% by 9:12 p.m. The next morning, I woke up with 48% battery, and that charge lasted through a similar routine, along with phone calls, texting and music and video streaming, before the battery finally died at 7:30 p.m.

The Duo has yet to give me a reason to stress about its battery life.

In a recent development, I will acknowledge I’m a tad pretentious when it comes to smartphone cameras. But if I’m documenting an event or photographing my fancy tea sets, I want the best cameras I can get. Unlike the Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models have a telephoto camera, more advanced optical zoom capabilities and larger main-camera sensors.

Industry observers note that most of the time, the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras do the trick just fine. Colors are vivid, details are sharp and images are bright. Videos look good, too, though the 18 Pro Max does a noticeably better job with nighttime footage, which can look more muddy on the Duo. Digital video on the Duo also tops out at 6x, versus 24x on the Pros. Most of the time, though, I’m quite content with what I capture with the Duo’s cameras.

As I noted in my review, the under-display FaceTime camera on the inner screen isn’t great, but I never really take selfies using that camera. It feels much more natural to use the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen, which serves up sharp photos every time.

Sources indicate that the cover screen selfie camera plays a critical role in an enhancement that makes using the Duo even more seamless. In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera.

It has been revealed that in the absence of Face ID, which I have felt rather painfully, this has been a solid workaround, even if it’s not as secure as Apple’s biometric facial recognition and authentication system. You’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode when using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and to unlock the phone after leaving it alone for around 45 minutes. But a win is a win. (You can also unlock the Duo using an Apple Watch, but I don’t have one.).

Industry observers note that I’ll admit I still feel a little bashful when pulling out the Duo because of how much attention it drums up, despite being far from the first foldable phone. But its limited availability and hype paired with the unique design make it eye-catching, for better or worse. Using the Duo has led to some fun conversations, whether it’s with a sales associate as I pay for a pastry or with Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, who spotted the phone in my hand during an interview and geeked out over it. That’s been a fun side effect of using Apple’s first foldable in my everyday life.

I’ve been living dangerously without a case; I don’t want anything to detract from the phone’s sleek feel. This is one of those “do as I say, not as I do” moments, as I’d recommend slapping a case on a phone that costs nearly $2,000. I did put a tempered glass screen protector on the cover display to guard against scratches. I can feel its edge against the otherwise flush surface of the phone when I hold it open, but aesthetic sacrifices must be made.

The Duo isn’t perfect, even if I love using this phone. After holding Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, the iPhone Duo can feel slightly chunky. The Z Fold 8 measures 4.5mm thick when open and 9.7mm when closed. Meanwhile, the Duo is 5.2mm thick when open and 11.3mm when closed. It’s not a huge difference, but it makes me look forward to Apple hopefully slimming down the second-generation version, if and when it comes.

The Duo is also slightly heavier than the Z Fold 8, weighing 254 grams (compared to 201 grams for Samsung’s foldable). I’m always surprised when people remark how heavy the Duo is, but I think the reason I don’t share that sentiment is that I’m accustomed to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which weighs 249 grams.

Industry observers note that when the Duo is open in landscape orientation, I’m glad there’s an option to split the keyboard so it’s easier to type across the wider expanse, but I wish the swipe functionality worked in that configuration, too. It’s a little thing that would make a noticeable difference for those of us who rely heavily on swipe-to-text.

Sources indicate that one drawback of the Duo’s compact design is that some existing MagSafe wallets and other accessories won’t stick to the back without awkwardly jutting out. So you might have to invest in some newly introduced accessories specifically designed for the Duo.

Until the recent addition of face unlock, the Duo’s biggest drawback was the lack of Face ID. It’s a feature I’d expect on such a premium device, especially given that even the budget-focused iPhone 17E supports it.

Touch ID works reliably on the Duo, but it’s slow compared to fingerprint unlock on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which also supports facial recognition). And while the upcoming face unlock capability on the Duo isn’t an exact replacement for Face ID, which is more secure, it helps make accessing the phone’s contents more convenient and in line with the Duo’s modern aesthetics.

I’ve finished my homework: My review is done, and now, so is this one-month follow-up. What’s next?

Recent findings suggest that I’m not sure I’m ready to throw in the towel on Apple’s foldable just yet. The novelty of the iPhone Duo hasn’t worn off, and I’ve become quite used to my passport-size companion. It does just about everything I need, despite some slight imperfections, and it’s fun to use. It’s also amusing to see how people react when they see it in my hand.

Recent findings suggest that so for now, it looks like the Duo will remain my daily driver. Whether the honeymoon phase eventually wears off remains to be seen, but I’m not in any hurry to end this love affair.

Breaking: 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1083 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

Sources indicate that “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

It has been revealed that the report demonstrates how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse mentioned, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

In a recent development, greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson mentioned.

In a recent development, what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson said Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ latest top stressor.

It has been revealed that it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

Industry observers note that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report indicates 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the organization, human or AI,” Samson stated. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Sources indicate that samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

In a recent development, “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most important decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse remarked.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more key tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse said.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

It has been revealed that “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

By Sarah Sidlow – Nov 19, 2026 at 6:15AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Scottsdale Funds - Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF ›.

The Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF (VGSH -0.06%) provides government-backed security stability, whereas the iShares 1-5 Year Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF (IGSB -0.02%) offers higher income through diversified investment-grade corporate debt.

In a recent development, investors often choose between government and corporate debt based on their need for safety versus potential income. While both funds target the shorter end of the maturity curve, they offer distinct risk profiles. This analysis compares a fund backed by the U.S. government against one that captures yields from corporate borrowers.

It has been revealed that beta measures price volatility relative to the S&P 500; beta is calculated from monthly returns over the available fund history (up to five years). The 1-yr return represents total return over the trailing 12 months. Dividend yield is the trailing-12-month distribution yield.

Recent findings suggest that the Vanguard fund is slightly more affordable with its 0.03% expense ratio. However, the iShares fund provides a notably higher payout, reflecting the additional yield typically required by investors to hold corporate debt over government securities.

Industry observers note that the Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF holds 91 securities, focusing on debt issued by the U.S. Treasury with maturities between one and three years. It was launched in 2009. Vanguard Short-Term Treasury ETF has paid $2.19 per share over the trailing 12 months, which on its recent ~$57.6 share price works out to a 3.8% yield.

The iShares 1-5 Year Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF holds 4,807 securities, emphasizing high-quality corporate debt with remaining maturities ranging from one to five years. The fund is highly diversified -- no single position exceeds 0.29% of the portfolio. It was launched in 2007. iShares 1-5 Year Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF has paid $2.40 per share over the trailing 12 months, which on its recent ~$51.5 share price works out to a 4.7% yield.

For more guidance on ETF investing, check out the full guide at this link.

It has been revealed that income investors will likely be drawn to IGSB's 4.7% dividend yield, which is more than 4 times the S&P 500's current yield. But as is often the case, that higher payout comes with slightly higher risk. IGSB holds corporate debt, and companies theoretically face a greater risk of defaulting on their loans than the U.S. government. That noted, IGSB's portfolio of nearly 5,000 holdings and its focus on high-quality debt mitigates a good deal of that risk.

Sources indicate that VGSH is likely the better play for investors looking for maximum capital preservation. Moreover, its massive size will appeal to conservative investors who are looking for maximum liquidity. Plus, the interest from U.S. Treasuries is usually exempt from state and local taxes, which could appeal to high earners.

It has been revealed that the shorter maturities for short-term bond funds mean investors are shielded from interest rate fluctuations, and these vehicles typically generate more income than cash or money market funds. For most investors looking to juice their passive income, IGSB is a solid choice. But if you're looking for extra security or have specific tax considerations, the short-term Treasuries in VGSH could be right for you.

Industry News: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Out. Here’s How to Make Room on Your Console

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive.
  • If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game.
  • In a recent development, the simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The wait is over. Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, and it is massive. The game is 212 GB, which means it takes up about half of the storage space on my Xbox Series S. The company confirmed that GTA 6 is available to stream via Xbox Cloud Gaming without downloading it to your console. However, cloud streaming GTA 6 might affect the game’s performance and relies heavily on a strong internet connection. To avoid those issues, I plan on downloading the game.

If you’re like me and are excited to play GTA 6 but don’t have much storage space, you have a few options: delete games, upgrade your console’s hard drive and streaming the game. Here’s what you should know about these options.

In a recent development, the simplest and cheapest way to free up space on your console for Grand Theft Auto 6 is to delete files and other games, which is what I’ll be doing. Uninstalling games is a good choice for folks who plan on spending a lot of time with GTA 6 and don’t intend to juggle different games. Rob Nelson, who oversees Rockstar North with Aaron Garbut, told The New York Times that he had an 80-hour playthrough of the game in February, so you can easily stay immersed in Grand Theft Auto’s state of Leonida.

Recent findings suggest that you may not need to delete much – uninstalling a game like Call of Duty alone could free up nearly 315 GB, giving you enough digital storage for GTA 6. Since deleting files is almost instantaneous, you can quickly reclaim hard drive space. Because you don’t need to buy additional storage, you’ll also save a lot of money – storage prices are through the roof at the moment.

Ultimately, deleting games is a great option if you don’t want to spend any additional money or you don’t mind redownloading games later.

Industry observers note that if you proposal on hopping between GTA 6 and other games, or you don’t want to delete many of your downloaded titles, you can upgrade your console’s storage. Buying storage is more expensive than deleting files from your console, but benefit from being able to seamlessly hop between Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty or Madden.

In a recent development, you can use internal or external storage for your console, but you might have to move files between your internal and external storage to launch games. An internal hard drive lets you seamlessly play games. Xbox consoles rely on proprietary expansion cards from Seagate or SanDisk that plug into your console for additional storage. The PlayStation 5 uses M.2 solid-state drives, which are installed alongside the PS5’s built-in storage, and CNET’s David Carnoy recommends the Lexar NM 790 as a fast SSD with a straightforward installation process.

Sources indicate that there shouldn’t be any performance, quality or load-time differences between running games from installed storage expansion devices versus your console’s internal storage. Both expansion cards and SSDs can be expensive, especially when compared with deleting games.

You could also use an external hard drive to expand your storage, which can be cheaper than buying expansion cards and internal SSD upgrades – you may even have a compatible USB external drive sitting around that you can use. However, there are caveats around what games can and can’t be played directly from external HDDs.

For Xbox consoles, some older Xbox, Xbox 360 and Xbox One titles can be stored and played from external HDDs. But games optimized for Series X/S consoles can only be stored on HDDs and must be moved back to your internal drive to play. Similarly, the PlayStation 5 only lets you store PS5 games on external HDDs, while you can store and run PS4 games from external drives.

It has been revealed that therefore, using an external HDD requires playing digital musical chairs, moving current-gen games back and forth between your external hard drive and internal console storage in order to play them. The LaCie Rugged SSD4 earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award and could be a good option. If its price tag scares you, the Western Digital P10 offers more storage at a more economical price point.

Rockstar unveiled that GTA 6 is available to stream on the Xbox consoles – no download required – via Xbox Cloud Gaming, with some quality and time limitations. You’ll need to buy either an Xbox Game Pass plan or Cloud Gaming hours. Folks who don’t want to delete games or upgrade their console storage can stream GTA 6, but you’ll need an Xbox One or Series X/S console, you won’t get the highest visual quality and you will have to pay for more playtime hours if they run out. Streaming GTA 6 could help budget-conscious gamers who don’t want to upgrade from Xbox One consoles or who don’t have the allotted storage space on their devices.

According to recent reports, normally, you can stream many games on PCs, mobile devices and TVs or streaming devices using Xbox Cloud Gaming or Game Pass, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is limited to the Xbox One, Series S and Series X. Additionally, GTA 6 streaming quality is capped at Series S graphical settings. So if you have a Series X, consider deleting games or upgrading your storage to run the game locally with better graphics.

While you’ll need to install the full game on your console first, remote play for Xbox and PlayStation consoles lets you stream GTA 6 to other devices, like your phone, tablet, streaming device or TV.

If you’re willing to pay a little more for the convenience of having multiple games ready to play at a moment’s notice, Xbox expansion cards or an internal SSD for a PS5 are your best options. If you want a cheaper option and don’t mind moving game files around, an external hard drive could be for you. If you have Xbox Game Pass or Xbox Cloud Gaming, you could stream the game to your console without needing more storage space. However, the cheapest option is to delete games from your internal storage and redownload them later, which can be time-consuming.

It has been revealed that I chose the cheapest option and deleted a few games from my Xbox. I’m not planning on leaving GTA 6 any time soon.

In a recent development, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
