    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
    • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
    • Industry observers note that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

    If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

    Industry observers note that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

    If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

    Non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

    Recent findings suggest that neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold notes.

    While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

    “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” indicates Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

    Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley claims.

    Got some counter space and an itch for a newly introduced food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

    Sources indicate that “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

    Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

    While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold notes.

    According to recent reports, electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath states.

    In a recent development, gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

    That noted, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold states.

    In a recent development, for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, notes consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

    You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

    “Significant-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

    Recent findings suggest that many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

    It has been revealed that shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold states. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

    Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath claims. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

    It has been revealed that one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

    Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

    Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

    Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch states.

    Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

    Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

    Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

    Industry observers note that let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

    Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

    Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    #39111. Your AI Assistant Could Work For Someone Else

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (817 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Your AI Assistant Could Work For Someone Else

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • ​Last year, attackers went after about 30 organizations using an AI coding assistant.
    • According to recent reports, what interests me is how they caught it.
    • Industry observers note that that may not be the case next time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Yaron Kassner, Co-founder and CTO, Silverfort.

    ​Last year, attackers went after about 30 organizations using an AI coding assistant. They jailbroke it, told it that it worked for a security firm running defensive tests, and broke the attack into small jobs that each looked innocent on its own. The assistant did them.

    According to recent reports, what interests me is how they caught it. The attacker was using his own AI account. That meant the organization running the assistant could look across all of his sessions at once and see what those small jobs added up to. One party had the whole picture.

    Industry observers note that that may not be the case next time. The assistants our teams use every day make it easier to do the same thing.

    In many of these cases, the attacker brought his own AI to the job, and that is what gave him away. See the Google Threat Intelligence report for another set of examples. The account, billing and session history often sit with a provider who can eventually piece the story together.

    In a recent development, there is a simpler option available. An attacker who lands on a single machine, or who picks up a working set of credentials, is often standing right next to an assistant that is already installed, already trusted inside the network, and already being paid for by the victim. How convenient.

    Charlie Bell at Microsoft gave this a good name a year ago when he wrote about AI agents becoming double agents: an assistant doing exactly what it was built to do, for the wrong person.

    According to recent reports, the assistants that matter most here are the ordinary ones. Coding and productivity assistants have broad access because broad access is what makes them worth having. They act as the person who started them. They run commands, open files, and reach source code, cloud accounts and mail. That is the whole point of them, and teams are right to use them.

    It also means that whoever gives one instructions holds most of that person’s access. Right now, an assistant takes its instructions from whoever is at the keyboard. It has no way of knowing whether that is still the person it was set up for, and it was never designed to ask. The approval prompt is there to help the user think twice. It was not built to stop someone who should not be there.

    In a recent development, break an attack into small enough pieces and no single piece looks like an attack. Listing the accounts in a directory is an access review. Reading through a repository is code review. Checking which machines answer on the network is inventory work. Every one of those has a reason to be happening on a Tuesday afternoon.

    It has been revealed that now hand the pieces to different assistants, one job each. Every assistant sees only the task in front of it, and every task is fine. The attack only exists as an attack in the mind of the person who split it up, or in the context window of the attacker’s own agent back home.

    The moment that matters is the tool call. An assistant holds its access whatever it is asked to do, and the prompt only decides which of that access gets used. The place to put the attention is where the assistant reaches out to another system.

    In a recent development, today those calls go out carrying the standing permissions of the person the assistant was set up for, which means the whole of that person’s reach is available for any request that sounds reasonable. The alternative is to give the assistant an identity of its own, scoped to the work it is actually doing, and to require actions that matter to be approved by something the assistant cannot grant itself. An assistant can be talked into asking for anything. It cannot be talked into holding a credential it was never given.

    Industry observers note that human approval deserves the same thought. A prompt that appears on the machine the attacker is already sitting on is an approval he grants himself. To count for anything, it has to arrive somewhere else, on a separate device, with the person granting it proving who they are.

    There is a habit of mind worth changing too. Many of us now run two efforts: one to protect our AI, and one to defend against AI. We treat them as separate problems, with separate thinking and separate owners. In a coding assistant, they are the same problem, on the same machine, under the same login. As long as we approach it as two, we will keep designing controls for half of it.

    Industry observers note that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    • By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 19, 2026 at 7:15AM EST.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Erin Kennedy – Updated Nov 19, 2026 at 7:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Interactive Brokers Group ›.

    Industry observers note that choosing between Interactive Brokers Group (IBKR +2.81%) and S&P Global (SPGI -0.79%) requires understanding how these financial giants generate wealth. You must decide which business model offers the better path for your portfolio.

    Interactive Brokers serves as a technology-first gateway to global markets, while S&P Global provides the essential data and credit ratings that the world's capital markets depend upon for daily operations. This comparison explores their financial health, growth rates, and valuation multiples to help you determine which stock is the superior buy today.

    Industry observers note that interactive Brokers operates as a highly automated global broker, providing direct-access execution and clearing services across more than 175 markets. The company operates within the broader universe of financial stocks, offering clients the ability to trade in roughly 29 different currencies. Its client base includes hedge funds, proprietary trading firms, and over 4.4 million individual investors, with no single customer accounting for more than approximately 2% of commissions.

    Industry observers note that reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each manufacturer's latest full fiscal year. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $6.2 billion, reflecting growth of roughly 19.7%. This expansion helped Interactive Brokers achieve net income of close to $984 million, supported by a healthy net margin of approximately 15.9%.

    Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the tech giant demonstrates a conservative financial structure. The debt-to-equity ratio, a metric showing the relationship between total debt and the equity shareholders have in the business, was approximately 0. Free cash flow, which is the cash a company generates from its operations minus its capital spending, reached nearly $15.7 billion, while the current ratio of roughly 1.1 indicates Interactive Brokers has sufficient short-term assets to cover its immediate obligations.

    According to recent reports, S&P Global provides critical intelligence through its credit ratings, benchmarks, and data analytics used by governments and corporations worldwide. The tech giant is a key player in global commodity and energy markets, with nearly 44,500 employees across 43 countries helping to maintain its market-leading positions. Its revenue streams are highly diversified, catering to asset managers, institutional investors, and investment banks that rely on its proprietary workflow solutions.

    During the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, the organization generated revenue of approximately $15.3 billion, an increase of nearly 7.9% over the prior year. Profitability remains a core strength for the business, as evidenced by net income of nearly $4.5 billion. This resulted in a robust net margin of roughly 29.2%, showcasing the high profitability inherent in its data-driven business model.

    Based on its December 2025 balance sheet, S&P Global manages a balanced capital structure. Its debt-to-equity ratio, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, is approximately 0.5. The current ratio, a liquidity measure that compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, reached nearly 0.8, while the business generated nearly $5.5 billion in free cash flow, providing significant capital for reinvestment or shareholder returns.

    Industry observers note that interactive Brokers faces intense competition from established prime brokers and newer zero-commission online platforms. The tech giant is subject to complex international regulatory requirements, including potential changes in laws that govern prediction markets and brokerage activities. Furthermore, its heavy reliance on proprietary technology means that system failures, cyberattacks, or data privacy breaches could disrupt operations. Shareholders should also note that the founder maintains majority voting control, which could lead to potential conflicts of interest.

    According to recent reports, S&P Global faces high cybersecurity risks due to its central role in the global financial infrastructure and the massive scale of its digital operations. The firm must constantly innovate to keep pace with new artificial intelligence technologies that could change how financial data is consumed. It also carries significant legal and regulatory exposure related to its ratings and indexes businesses. Additionally, the company relies on third-party providers like Amazon (AMZN +1.69%) for cloud services.

    S&P Global appears more conservatively valued based on its lower multiple of future earnings estimates, while Interactive Brokers trades at a higher price for its faster growth.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

    Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

    It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

    The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

    Industry observers note that investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

    » MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    According to recent reports, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    By Anthony Di Pizio – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:16AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    The S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%) stock market index is down 3% from its high as I write this on Nov. 16. The technology-heavy Nasdaq-100 index is down even more sharply, having lost 10% of its peak value. While stocks typically trend higher over the long term, investors are adopting a cautious approach right now amid a growing chorus of risks.

    It has been revealed that last week, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped away from the company after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, one with an alleged Chinese spy. Formal investigations are still underway, but Nvidia is the most important company in the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem, so Huang's departure cast a cloud of uncertainty over the entire industry.

    According to recent reports, an elevated inflation rate also forced the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its September meeting, and more hikes are expected. In the past, rising rates alone have been enough to derail bull markets, so they could be a significant headwind for returns going forward.

    I think the stock market is especially vulnerable to a steep sell-off right now, but legendary investor Warren Buffett has some sound advice for navigating these very situations.

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang was integral to the success of not only Nvidia, but the entire AI industry. He used the company's vast resources to invest in countless AI start-ups, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which helped subsidize the significant costs associated with building data center infrastructure.

    Nvidia's current interim chief executive officer is Colette Kress, who previously served as the manufacturer's longtime chief financial officer. She is widely expected to be more conservative than Huang, at a time when many AI companies, especially neoclouds like CoreWeave (CRWV +8.59%), face soaring borrowing costs and more discerning equity investors. Without Nvidia's ongoing support, some of those companies could find themselves in a dire financial situation.

    Meanwhile, broader economic growth is also under threat. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation rose at an annualized rate of 3.7% in September, prompting the Federal Reserve to increase the federal funds rate (overnight interest rate) by 25 basis points at its September meeting.

    It has been revealed that the CPI then rose at an estimated annualized rate of 4% in October (an official set of year-over-year data is unavailable due to the government shutdown in October 2025), putting more rate hikes in play. In fact, the CME Group's FedWatch tool indicates there is a certain chance of another hike in December, followed by two more hikes in 2027. FedWatch calculates the probability of interest rate moves by analyzing the 30-day fed funds futures market, so it tends to be a reliable indicator.

    Rising interest rates force consumers to allocate more of their household budgets to debt repayments, leaving less money for discretionary spending. Moreover, companies tend to think twice about borrowing money to fuel their expansion plans when rates are high. If these headwinds persist for long enough, they can weigh on corporate earnings, and earnings tend to drive stock prices.

    Industry observers note that during the Fed's last rate-hiking cycle, which spanned from March 2022 to August 2023, the S&P 500 suffered a bear-market decline of more than 20%. A similar result is certainly possible this time around, particularly when combined with the jitters in the AI industry.

    It has been revealed that warren Buffett served as the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway from 1965 to 2025. Had you invested $1,000 in Berkshire stock when he took the helm and never sold, it would have been worth a staggering $48 million by the time he stepped down. Simply put, Buffett knew how to pick winning acquisitions for Berkshire's portfolio.

    Recent findings suggest that in his 1986 letter to Berkshire's shareholders, Buffett famously mentioned, "We simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy, and be greedy only when others are fearful." In other words, he stockpiled cash during periods of euphoria in the markets, and deployed that money aggressively during severe downturns. He always believed the long-term uptrend in the broader market would prevail over time, which gave him conviction.

    Sources indicate that buffett also liked to remind investors that stocks represent real businesses with real fundamentals. They aren't just financial instruments that move up and down -- a person wouldn't sell their house if its value dropped during a given year, so selling a stock for the same reason makes little sense. As long as the underlying business remains healthy, a falling stock price should be viewed as a chance to buy more.

    Therefore, while stock market declines can be unsettling, investors might want to prepare to put some money to work.

    #39105. AI Is Making The Handoff Optional

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1016 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    AI Is Making The Handoff Optional

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1016 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Swapnil Upganlawar, Senior Leader in generative AI at Amazon Web Services (AWS).
    • Some of the boundaries that AI agents are beginning to cross are the same ones I spent years building enterprise software to manage.
    • Early in my career, I worked on enterprise service-management products built around ITIL, a framework for IT service management.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Swapnil Upganlawar, Senior Leader in generative AI at Amazon Web Services (AWS).

    Some of the boundaries that AI agents are beginning to cross are the same ones I spent years building enterprise software to manage.

    Early in my career, I worked on enterprise service-management products built around ITIL, a framework for IT service management. Machine learning was already part of my work. These products supported interconnected business services, where changing one component could affect others.

    Building for those environments meant thinking beyond whether an individual operation succeeded. Someone needed to understand its effect on the service, own the consequences and know how to recover when something went wrong.

    It has been revealed that that experience gave me respect for organizational boundaries. Different teams held different expertise and authority. Passing work between them could be essential. But it also made the dependency between technology and process hard to miss: When systems could not share information, people had to carry it.

    Recent findings suggest that as my ML work expanded into recommendation and personalization systems, I began addressing another part of that problem. We built ways to help people find relevant knowledge and make better decisions without searching through everything themselves. A useful recommendation still left a person with the work of acting on it.

    My responsibilities also spanned program management and engineering. I saw the work between a good idea and a delivered result. Resolving dependencies, negotiating priorities and deciding which commitments could be kept were substantial parts of the job. So was the less rewarding work of collecting information from one group and translating it for another. Some of that coordination requires leadership. Some exists because information and systems are fragmented.

    Recent findings suggest that that distinction became more consequential when I led AI transformation across the employee life cycle for a workforce of 1.3 million people. The work spanned onboarding, ongoing support and departure. I led teams across science, engineering, product and program management, bringing responsibility for the employee experience and its supporting systems into the same leadership scope. We were now trying to resolve needs that crossed several departments.

    In a recent development, imagine an employee moving into a new role. The reporting line changes, but access permissions do not. The employee supplies the details to one team, then another asks for them again. Each department may be completing its part correctly. The person still cannot get started. That is why I think about the whole journey when assessing an AI improvement. A better answer is valuable. The employee also needs the organization to follow through.

    Today, I lead a portfolio of five enterprise AI products spanning intelligent search, managed knowledge retrieval, business assistants and agentic workflows. Search helps locate knowledge scattered across systems. Managed retrieval helps ground AI responses in organizational information. Business assistants make that knowledge easier to use. Agents can connect it to actions, as long as they have the right tools and authority.

    Industry observers note that my job is to make those connections dependable. The goal is to let other teams build useful AI experiences without reconstructing the foundations for finding and using enterprise knowledge each time.

    According to recent reports, recent agent releases combine persistent execution, reusable skills and context across applications. Those advertised capabilities need testing in each workflow, but they make it reasonable to ask whether another handoff is necessary.

    We could have removed some of that work years ago. AI should not get credit for a process we never bothered to simplify. The more interesting opportunity involves requests that arrive incomplete, require interpretation or depend on several kinds of expertise.

    Recent findings suggest that A 2025 product-development experiment gives us one reason to examine those boundaries. Individuals using AI matched the performance of two-person teams without it and spent 16.4% less time than the control group. AI also helped participants combine technical and commercial perspectives. That is evidence about a particular task, not a staffing formula. It suggests that some work we habitually divide into successive contributions may be worth organizing differently.

    According to recent reports, the coordination can also reappear elsewhere. An October 2026 study inside an AI developer found that “meta-work,” including managing agents and building supervision tools, rose from 10% to 22% of employees’ interactive AI sessions. Meeting time among technical individual contributors increased 16% over the previous year. The findings describe one rapidly growing workplace and do not establish that AI caused the increase in meetings. Before calling a workflow simpler, I want to know where that work went.

    Having led both program management and engineering, I expect some responsibilities we right now separate to come together. Someone who can use AI to investigate a problem, test an approach and coordinate routine execution may be able to own more of the outcome. That requires changes in authority and incentives. If people are rewarded only for completing their department’s portion, they have little reason to simplify the whole process. I would give the person responsible for the outcome the authority to challenge unnecessary handoffs and judge the result across the entire journey.

    Sources indicate that for employees changing roles, I would review each handoff with the people responsible for it. Reentering a verified start date is a reasonable candidate for removal. Authorizing access to sensitive records needs a different standard. The person performing a seemingly redundant check may know exactly which mistake it prevents. I would also keep someone accountable for the complete request, including exceptions. Otherwise, departmental queues could become agent queues, with the employee still chasing progress. The measures should follow that person: time to completion, repeated requests for information, corrections and whether they can actually do their upcoming job.

    My early experience building enterprise service-management products still shapes this approach. Ownership, reliability and recovery remain essential. What deserves reconsideration is every transfer that adds no expertise, decision or protection.

    If AI makes every team faster but the employee still waits just as long, what have we actually improved?

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    More than four months after the news broke that Miami Heat substantial man Bam Adebayo punched Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro, Adebayo delivered another blow against Herro — this one in the form of a vindicating 21 first-half points in their first game between one another.

    During a Wednesday night showdown rich with storylines, Adebayo at one point scored nine in a row and connected on a trio of 3-pointers over the opening two quarters.

    Recent findings suggest that of course, all the while, Giannis Antetokounmpo was facing the team he was synonymous with for 13 seasons. And the matchup was taking place in Miami's Kaseya Center, which doubled as "Vice City" on the eve of the highly anticipated nationwide release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

    Industry observers note that antetokounmpo played the facilitator role with nine assists and still managed 27 points in the Heat's 137-130 victory over the Bucks. Adebayo finished with 26 points. Herro, meanwhile, was booed throughout and clocked out with just eight points on 4-of-11 shooting.

    Sources indicate that miami (9-6) has now won six consecutive games after a 3-6 start. Milwaukee (1-14), on the other hand, remains dead last in the East.

    Herro is a Milwaukee native, but Miami is where he began his NBA career. In that way, Wednesday was a homecoming for him. The same could be said for Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis, who also started their NBA journeys with the Heat before being shipped off to the Bucks in the Antetokounmpo trade.

    The blockbuster deal also delivered the Bucks the 13th overall pick in this year's draft — which they used to select Tennessee forward Nate Ament — as well as future draft considerations, including two more first-round picks.

    In addition to Antetokounmpo, the Heat received Bobby Portis, who became a fan favorite in Milwaukee while helping the "Greek Freak" lead the franchise to its first NBA championship in 50 years back in 2021.

    The end of Antetokounmpo's tenure with the Bucks was dominated by drama, particularly as the two-time league MVP and 10-time All-Star feuded with the organization over his health.

    Miami gave him a fresh start, and the Antetokounmpo-piloted Heat are taking off under longtime head coach Erik Spoelstra.

    Herro's Bucks are on the other end of the NBA spectrum, clearly entrenched in a Taylor Jenkins-directed rebuild. Herro heard the jeers of Miami fans over the course of the night.

    Even though he won NBA Sixth Man of the Year during the 2021-22 campaign and earned All-Star recognition with the Heat in the 2024-25 season, his reputation in Miami took a hit this offseason.

    Critical commentary Herro shared about Adebayo on social media led to the infamous physical altercation between the former teammates in Las Vegas ahead of Summer League action. They shared the floor together in Miami from 2019-26. In that span, the Heat made a pair of NBA Finals appearances.

    But there was ostensibly no love lost by the end of that seven-season stretch. As reported in July by the Miami Herald, around that time, Herro posted a graphic on Instagram that listed the league's worst midrange shooters last season. Antetokounmpo topped that unfortunate leaderboard at 26.8%, and Adebayo came in 10th at 35.9%, per the Herald.

    Plus, screenshots circulated of a direct message conversation, in which comments seemingly questioning Adebayo's play and contract were attributed to Herro online.

    Herro noted shortly after the dustup that he wanted to "move on" from the incident, except it was top of mind for everyone watching Wednesday's game.

    Adebayo stated afterward that he didn't get to talk to Herro but that he's not someone who holds grudges. He noted that he's "on to the next thing.".

    "I feel like I got great karma," Adebayo added, via Will Manso of WPLG Local 10 News.

    In a recent development, adebayo's nine straight points arrived in the second quarter. He capped that surge by stepping in front of a pass from Jaquez and turning the steal into a two-handed flush that staked Miami to a 48-28 advantage.

    The Heat were in control from the jump. They went 22 of 48 from 3, including 13 of 28 in the first half. Klay Thompson continued his hot streak with four triples and 13 points.

    Recent findings suggest that antetokounmpo orchestrated several of the team's 3-pointers. His dribble-drive penetration set the stage for kickouts, most notably a no-look dish that rewarded Adebayo early on.

    Industry observers note that antetokounmpo's first points didn't come until the 5:11 mark of the first quarter. His first field goal gave the Heat their 70th point. In the process, though, he had an effect that extended far beyond his scoring.

    Maybe his most impressive moment was when he rose up to deny Bucks rookie guard Brayden Burries with a two-handed rejection at the rim late in the second quarter.

    In the third quarter, Antetokounmpo swung a shrewd shovel pass to Andrew Wiggins, who promptly cashed in from long range.

    Then Antetokounmpo slammed home a lob from Adebayo, showing off what they can do in the two-man game.

    Sources indicate that antetokounmpo stacked 14 rebounds and ended up an assist shy of a triple-double. He told reporters postgame that he didn't think it felt weird facing Milwaukee.

    In a recent development, "Look, I think since I was a kid, when I play basketball, I try to lock in as much as I can," Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic's Eric Nehm. "People that have been around me know how I operate on game days. I try not to say much. I try not to interact as much. And the only thing on my mind is, 'How can I help my team win and how can I do my job?' It doesn't matter who I play.

    According to recent reports, "… I could have been playing against my four brothers and my two sons. It doesn't matter. I try to do my best and try to do the things that I've worked on and try to have fun. It doesn't matter what uniform I go against.".

    His old team made made things look closer than they actually were down the stretch. The Bucks were paced by Kyle Kuzma (26 points), Burries (20) and Jakučionis (20).

    Milwaukee is a ways from competing for a playoff spot again, whereas Miami is shaping up to be a threat in the Eastern Conference, just like the Bucks were all those years with Antetokounmpo.

    The franchises are linked because of this summer's trade and what happened in its aftermath.

    And on Wednesday, the Heat led by as many as 30 points, as Antetokounmpo and Adebayo flexed their value.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Emma Newbery – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:22AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Caterpillar ›.

    In a recent development, anthropic's (ANT +0.00%) initial public offering (IPO) looks set to be another blockbuster, possibly setting new IPO records and giving investors a chance to access a pure-play artificial intelligence (AI) stock. However, large IPOs can be speculative, and history tells us they often fall in their first year.

    Anthropic's prospectus notes a lot about both AI's huge potential and enormous risks. Putting the potential existential risks to humanity to one side, one figure struck me: It disclosed over $900 billion in planned compute and infrastructure spending. It says it will spend more than half of that before the end of 2030. As a relatively cautious investor, I'm more excited by that solid commitment than the initial volatility of an IPO.

    While many of Anthropic's deals are not public or are subcontracted through its partners, these industrial stocks already have Anthropic funds and are set to benefit from further AI infrastructure spending.

    NYSE · As of 9:37 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Already an AI pick-and-shovel favorite, Caterpillar (CAT +0.53%) soared to an all-time high of over $1,070 in June. However, at the time of this writing on Nov. 18, the stock is trading close to $560 -- almost 50% down from its high and little changed for the year. The well-known brand manufactures industrial equipment, including gas turbines and power generators.

    Its Q3 sales increased 17% from the year before to $20.7 billion, coming in just above analyst estimates. Some of that has been driven by the significant power demands of data centers and cloud computing. Indeed, one striking figure from its earnings is its record $78 billion backlog, reflecting robust demand across the board and giving the tech giant a cushion against possible slowdowns in AI spending.

    That backlog brings me to Anthropic, which essentially paid to jump the queue by taking over OnePWR's Caterpillar order for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generators. Anthropic paid $3.4 billion to take over the orders, which are expected to be available in the next two years. The deal, completed in September, highlights how important power-generation equipment is to AI firms, and bodes well for Caterpillar's growth.

    NYSE · As of 9:40 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Vertiv (VRT +2.71%) keeps data center equipment cool. It manufactures power management technology and cooling systems that allow data centers to process high computing workloads. This week, it expanded its 800-volt direct current (VDC) systems, which were developed in collaboration with Nvidia (NVDA +3.88%) and are designed to better support the needs of next-generation data centers. It is a key development that should help Vertiv maintain its dominant position.

    According to recent reports, vertiv's modular designs can reduce the time it takes to bring data centers online -- an attractive proposition in the race to build massive AI infrastructure as fast as possible. However, fears that the pace of data center development may slow and questions about the sustainability of the AI boom have weighed on Vertiv shares. Its stock is trading around $197, 48% lower than its May all-time high. Despite its falling share price, Vertiv's Q3 results beat expectations with quarterly sales up 61% year-on-year to $4.3 billion. The firm also stated that its Q3 orders were up over 100% from the year before.

    Anthropic's $900 billion spending spree suggests the AI build-out has room to run, which would be good for Vertiv demand.

    Recent findings suggest that crucially, Anthropic doesn't want to rely on leasing cloud capacity; it is investing in its own purpose-built data centers, powered by specialized chips. Vertiv is a major AI infrastructure player, but its connection to Anthropic is somewhat indirect. It is a partner in Hut 8's (HUT +7.03%) River Bend data center campus in Louisiana, which The Financial Times reports will supply 245 megawatts of computing power to Anthropic.

    NYSE · As of 9:39 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Industry observers note that with a market cap of around $2 billion, ERock (EROC +3.54%), is smaller and significantly riskier than Vertiv or Caterpillar. The firm boasts its ability to provide reliable off-grid generators quickly, which can later transition into backup power.

    According to recent reports, ERock itself IPO'd in June, and has had a bumpy first six months. It went public with an offer price of $21.50 and is now trading at $7.58. Given its relative youth and size, ERock's contract to provide 470 megawatts of power equipment to Anthropic is significant. Its RockBlock generators run primarily on natural gas. It's worth noting that Anthropic points to the importance of natural gas several times in its IPO prospectus, specifically the increased competition for supply and pipeline capacity.

    All three of these industrial firms have existing ties with Anthropic and are part of massive AI infrastructure developments already underway. The demand and strong order books are attractive, and the recent investor caution on AI means their share prices are now more reasonably priced. There is still risk, and caution is justified, but none of them depend only on the AI build-out, and all could benefit from Anthropic's huge spending looks.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TMF Breakfast News – Nov 19, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.

    It has been revealed that anthropic (ANT +0.00%) enters the public market as one of the 10 most valuable companies in America, with growth few businesses have matched and computing bills few could afford. The company behind the Claude artificial intelligence (AI) models begins trading on the Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT after pricing its shares at $83 last night, above its expected range of $70 to $78. This makes Anthropic worth about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

    Recent findings suggest that buy Now or Wait? Where Our Teams Stand.

    It has been revealed that team Hidden Gems’ 5-year price target is $214.78, and Team Rule Breakers’ is $160, both well above Anthropic’s IPO price of $83 a share. Both teams admire Anthropic’s growth and share the same caution over its costs and governance, and they differ mainly on timing.

    Recent findings suggest that team Hidden Gems is taking a position now, since few companies of any size have grown as fast as Anthropic. Team Rule Breakers wants to review a few quarters of public results first and see a clear path to sustained profitability.

    Recent findings suggest that “This IPO looks very different from SpaceX’s (SPCX +1.60%) debut in June. SpaceXwent public at about 94 times its 2025 revenue, its AI segment was losing billions, and much of the hype was (and still is) focused on future revenue streams that haven't materialized yet. Anthropic, on the other hand, has already reported its first quarterly operating profit and, at the top end of its price range, would be valued at about 29 times trailing revenue. That's less than one-third of SpaceX's IPO sales multiple, for a business growing many times faster.”.

    Asit Sharma, Team Rule Breakers.

    Recent findings suggest that “Over time, Anthropic's cost structure will smooth itself out. But we'd like to see a clear path to sustained profitability, especially as it starts to lay out cash for the massive $450 billion in computing capacity it wants to obtain for the next four years alone. Team Rule Breakers believes it prudent to review the next few quarters' results before considering taking a position, and frankly, we're excited to dig into future filings; after all, Anthropic already breaks so many rules with superior results.”.

    What Every Investor Should Know.

    According to recent reports, 1. Businesses can’t get enough of Claude. Anthropic charges companies based on how much they use Claude for coding and office work, and usage has exploded. Revenue reached $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, about 13 times the same stretch a year earlier. Customers from a year ago now spend about nine times as much, and more than half the Fortune 500 spend at least $100,000 a year with Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, 2. Computing costs are the swing factor. Running Claude takes enormous computing power, and Anthropic rents most of it through long-term contracts. In Q3, demand outgrew those contracts, so the company rented pricier short-term capacity, and computing costs rose to 58% of revenue from 48% in Q2. Anthropic remained profitable on an adjusted basis, but with about $70 billion of computing bills due in the next year and roughly $900 billion committed overall, revenue has to keep growing swiftly.

    3. The price assumes years of fast growth. The IPO values Anthropic at about 43 times trailing sales on a fully diluted basis, less than half SpaceX’s multiple at its June debut, though that still leaves little room for error if growth slows. ANT’s first few months may also be bumpy, since up to 315 million insider shares can be sold starting today and index funds may have to buy within weeks.

    According to recent reports, 4. Public investors get almost no say. The seven co-founders control 50.1% of the vote, and an independent trust picks most of the board. If you’d rather not pay up for a tech giant you can’t influence, you likely already own a piece of Anthropic through Amazon (AMZN +1.56%) and Alphabet (GOOGL +2.92%), which own sizable stakes and supply much of its computing power.

    #39096. Your AI Agents Are Getting Phished, And Waiting To Respond Won't Save Them

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Your AI Agents Are Getting Phished, And Waiting To Respond Won't Save Them

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • IRONSCALES founder & CEO Eyal Benishti is a pioneering security software engineer & executive leader with 15+ years of industry experience.
    • Recent findings suggest that ​For decades, phishing has had one target: people.
    • Sources indicate that inboxes have a fresh reader: AI agents.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    IRONSCALES founder & CEO Eyal Benishti is a pioneering security software engineer & executive leader with 15+ years of industry experience.

    Recent findings suggest that ​For decades, phishing has had one target: people. Every line of defense we’ve constructed, from filters to awareness training, assumed a human sat at the end of the chain. For the attack to work, someone had to click the link, open the attachment, provide the credentials or approve the wire transfer. That window between delivery and action is where detection did its work. Models that learn how people normally communicate could spot what looked off and stop the threat before anyone acted.

    Sources indicate that inboxes have a fresh reader: AI agents. And these agents are being given real autonomy, including the ability to summarize messages, file tickets, move documents and even trigger workflows on employees’ behalf. They work promptly, they don’t second-guess themselves, and attackers have started to take notice.

    In such an environment, traditional detection and response approaches to defense begin to break down. When attacks can succeed without any human intervention at all, it’s imperative that organizations adapt to a more preemptive approach to cybersecurity.

    Recent findings suggest that the scale of this shift is hard to overstate. In a survey of 501 U.S. IT and security leaders from Censuswide and commissioned by my manufacturer, 96% said their organizations use AI agents or tools that can take actions on behalf of employees. And more than half (52%) said that use is widespread across the organization.

    Industry observers note that these agents aren’t confined to performing innocuous tasks. Many can access and interact with ticketing systems, HR services, cloud storage, internal files, security tools and, in some cases, payment systems.

    And attackers are exploiting that access. In the same survey, 77% of respondents said that in the past year, an AI agent at their organization acted on instructions or content that turned out to be malicious, misleading or unauthorized. This isn’t some threat looming beyond the horizon. It’s already here, and already making its presence felt.

    In a recent development, the most common way these agents are being exploited today is a familiar one. Among organizations that had an incident, the top type was an AI tool summarizing or acting on a malicious email or message. Phishing hasn’t gone anywhere; it’s just found a upcoming target. A malicious message no longer has to fool an employee. It only has to fool the agent sitting between that employee and their inbox.

    Most security teams already automate what they trust to run on its own. Detection flags the message, remediation pulls it, and an analyst reviews the calls that need judgment. Teams set those thresholds deliberately, because someone has to answer for every automated action. That design works when the attacker’s message waits for a person to act on it, which gives the team a window to catch up.

    It has been revealed that agents close that window. Even with solid email security in place, the occasional convincing phishing email still lands in an inbox. A person might open it seconds, minutes or hours later. An agent reads it on arrival, interprets the instructions and acts, often before anyone on the team knows the message exists.

    By the time an alert fires or an analyst reviews the verdict, the agent may have downloaded the file, shared the data, changed the account or queued the payment. Faster response helps, and so does tighter automation, but anything that runs after the agent reads the message arrives second. With an agent, the action is the damage.

    Sources indicate that detection still matters, and it has to run ahead of the agent’s first move. Your existing response process, automated and human, then serves as the backstop for what slips through.​.

    In a recent development, preemptive security flips the model of detection and response. Instead of waiting for an attack and racing to contain it, organizations anticipate threats, remove exposure and neutralize malicious content before it reaches its target, human or machine. In practice, that means five shifts:.

    If agents have access to email, the inbox is now an input to your business systems. Malicious content must be stopped before a person or an agent acts on it, which requires defenses that go beyond recognizing known bad links and attachments and actually understand intent and context.

    Industry observers note that attackers research their targets before they strike, and defenders should, too. Map what an outsider can learn about your people, vendors and operations, then use those findings to harden defenses and prepare employees before a real campaign begins.

    An agent that can read email and act on behalf of the inbox’s owner, with all the same permissions, is a upcoming user with real power. Give agents only the access their tasks require, monitor what they do, and keep records that show clearly who, or what, did what.

    In many organizations, IT approves new agents with little input from security. But deciding what an agent can touch is a risk decision, and it belongs with the people whose job is to anticipate abuse.

    Recent findings suggest that phishing simulations and red-team exercises should include attacks aimed at agents, not only at employees. Confidence in a initiative is not proof that it works.

    None of this means abandoning detection and response altogether. Some threats will still get through, and teams need the ability to investigate and respond in a timely manner. But detection can no longer be the primary strategy. It has to be the backstop.

    AI agents will keep spreading throughout the enterprise because the productivity gains are too enticing. Attackers know this, and they’re already testing how easily those agents can be turned against the organizations that deploy them. In the age of agentic AI, the advantage goes to whoever gets the first step, and defenders can’t afford to fall behind.​​.

    #39093. Industry News: How Smarter AI Could Reshape The Future Of Surgical Robots

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1022 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: How Smarter AI Could Reshape The Future Of Surgical Robots

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ming-Chien Chyu, PhD, PE, Founding President, Healthcare Engineering Alliance Society (HEALS), and professor at Texas Tech University.
    • Recent findings suggest that in 2025, researchers reported SRT-H, a hierarchical AI system that autonomously performed steps of cholecystectomy on eight ex vivo gallbladders.
    • That raises a broader design question: As AI takes on more functions, what should the surgeon, AI, robot and instrument each be responsible for?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ming-Chien Chyu, PhD, PE, Founding President, Healthcare Engineering Alliance Society (HEALS), and professor at Texas Tech University.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2025, researchers reported SRT-H, a hierarchical AI system that autonomously performed steps of cholecystectomy on eight ex vivo gallbladders. While limited to a single procedure in an ex vivo setting, it suggests how substantial new capability can come from intelligence controlling an existing robotic platform.

    That raises a broader design question: As AI takes on more functions, what should the surgeon, AI, robot and instrument each be responsible for?

    I propose answering that question capability by capability, determining where each function belongs: with the surgeon, AI, robot or instrument.

    Clinical judgment, oversight and critical decisions should remain centered on the surgeon. AI can increasingly assist with perception, planning, guidance and carefully bounded tasks. The robotic platform provides positioning, motion control and the mechanical stability, precision and safety functions that must remain physically enforced, while instruments provide physical interaction with tissue.

    Where a capability belongs depends partly on whether it must work if higher-level software fails, whether it varies among procedures or patients, whether it can be reliably validated and monitored and how difficult it is to modify once physically built into a system.

    Recent findings suggest that force sensing illustrates the trade-off. AI-based virtual sensing could potentially estimate some tool-tissue forces from information already available to the system, reducing reliance on dedicated sensors in appropriate applications. But estimated forces carry uncertainty and may suit some assistive functions better than safety-critical ones. Some capabilities may migrate toward AI; others remain fundamentally physical. Software cannot give an instrument a physical degree of freedom it lacks.

    Mechanical limits, emergency stops and some redundant safeguards should remain independent.

    AI can optimize within the safety envelope; it should not necessarily define it.

    According to recent reports, nor does this imply one universal robot. Bone resection, laparoscopy and endoluminal procedures have different mechanical requirements. The principle is more realistically applied within compatible surgical classes: Decide where each capability belongs, then design the system accordingly.

    In a recent development, capability allocation and responsibility allocation are closely related. For every capability assigned to AI, developers, regulators and clinicians must also determine who has authority over that function and who remains accountable when it fails.

    Sources indicate that telesurgery adds another dimension to the allocation question: where the AI itself should reside. Latency and network reliability remain notable challenges in telesurgery. Surgical AI could reside with the remote expert, locally with the patient and robot, or be distributed between both locations. That choice could affect latency, autonomy, safety, responsibility and handoff.​.

    Recent findings suggest that smarter AI does not automatically reduce cost. Costs include instruments, service and training, while AI introduces development, validation, cybersecurity and life cycle costs. Moving versatility into software may lower some costs while creating others.

    The real question is whether better capability allocation and smarter AI can improve efficiency, consistency and outcomes while reducing the total cost of delivering safe, high-quality robotic surgery.

    Savings from reduced hardware complexity or operating-room requirements would need to outweigh additional software, regulatory and life cycle costs.

    Research on autonomy in robotic surgery highlights limited access to high-quality surgical data, difficulties modeling deformable tissues and validating increasingly autonomous systems.

    The challenge is not simply collecting more data, but building curated diversity in datasets with reduced errors while preserving clinically meaningful variations in anatomy, pathology, technique and unexpected events. Expert clinical annotation can help distinguish noise from meaningful variation, while multi-institutional data broaden representation. Simulation and synthetic data can supplement unusual scenarios but cannot yet fully reproduce biological complexity.

    The FDA’s 2025 final guidance on predetermined change control prepares (PCCPs) allows manufacturers to specify planned modifications to AI-enabled devices and how they will be developed and validated; changes outside an authorized plan may require additional regulatory review. The FDA’s 2026 draft guidance for robotically assisted surgical devices separately addresses controls, reliability, software, cybersecurity and other system requirements.

    AI modularity therefore requires regulatory and validation boundaries as well as technical ones.

    The key question is when autonomy should end and control should return to the surgeon.

    The system should be able to detect and signal when it is operating outside its validated range, and then transition control according to a predefined handoff protocol. Determining when control should return to the surgeon remains a central challenge for autonomous robotic surgery.

    In many proposed autonomous systems, an AI-controlled task could be required to stop when the AI’s own estimate of confidence falls below a validated threshold. But an AI system can be highly confident and still be wrong, and recognizing unfamiliar conditions remains challenging. Other potential handoff triggers include observed anatomy deviating sufficiently from expectation or an action approaching a predefined safety boundary. These are proposed triggers, not established clinical thresholds.

    An equally crucial challenge is what happens after AI’s handoff. A surgeon taking control mid-task must rapidly understand what the system has done, why it stopped and what requires attention.

    Autonomy is not defined only by what a system can do but also by how safely it gives control back when it reaches its limits.

    The handoff function should therefore be treated as a safety-critical capability, not merely an AI feature.

    Industry observers note that A useful lesson may come from autonomous driving systems, where safe human takeover has become a central design challenge. In surgery, designing the handoff may ultimately prove as important as designing the autonomy itself.

    The future of robotic surgery may depend not only on smarter AI but also on determining where each capability can be delivered most safely, reliably and economically.

    For every capability proposed for AI, ask:.

    • What independent safeguard remains if the software fails?

    • Across what patient cohorts, procedures and conditions has it been validated?

    • What triggers the handoff, what does the surgeon see and what can the surgeon do when AI stops?

    If developers cannot answer all three, that capability is not ready to move into AI.​.

    #39089. From AI Tools To AI Development Systems: How To Build A Better Software Engineering Process

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1009 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    From AI Tools To AI Development Systems: How To Build A Better Software Engineering Process

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1009 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Roman Eloshvili is the Founder and CEO of XData Group, a B2B software development manufacturer with a focus on the European banking sector.
    • AI coding tools have thoroughly changed the way engineers work, making it possible to generate code and build features much faster than we used to be able to do by hand alone.
    • It has been revealed that I’ve already mentioned in the past that simply writing code is not the same as actually putting reliable software into production.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Roman Eloshvili is the Founder and CEO of XData Group, a B2B software development manufacturer with a focus on the European banking sector.

    AI coding tools have thoroughly changed the way engineers work, making it possible to generate code and build features much faster than we used to be able to do by hand alone. But now we face a bigger question: How do we build development processes around those tools?​.

    It has been revealed that I’ve already mentioned in the past that simply writing code is not the same as actually putting reliable software into production. With AI becoming the fastest part of the engineering process, it can actually lead to entirely new problems if testing, security and human decision-making don’t keep up.​.

    In a recent development, it’s not enough to simply plug an AI coding tool into an existing setup and expect everything else to stay the same. The process on the whole also needs to change. According to a report published by GitLab earlier in 2026, roughly 79% of developers claim that AI has greatly boosted code output, yet despite this greater productivity, the overall software delivery cycle has not become faster.​.

    That’s why I believe the next logical step here is to move away from individual tools and toward a more complete AI development system.​.

    The short and direct answer is: decisions. It’s crucial to understand that AI does not make engineers obsolete—it just changes where their focus needs to be. AI can handle a lion’s share of technical work, but it doesn’t decide what a business should actually build and why. That still belongs in the hands of the people leading that company.​.

    At the same time, there are also things AI simply cannot do on its own because they involve human-to-human interactions in the real world. For example, a model can build a mobile application, but someone still needs to open it on an actual device and check if everything works as intended from the user’s perspective. This cannot be done through automation alone.​.

    Sources indicate that even when a release is ready to go into production, it still needs to go through approvals and external reviews. A submission to place your app in App Store or Google Play, once again, can’t be handled by AI. Human oversight and engagement are still necessary at these stages.​.

    Sources indicate that the rest of the process, on the other hand, can become much more automated. Once the business requirements and the specifications for the necessary piece of software have been established, AI can generate the code, another AI will review it and then the result can be put through a smoke test to make sure all the core functions are in the clear.​.

    The main point is this: The human engineer no longer needs to read every line of code—that would just defeat the point of using AI at this scale. So instead, their attention moves to decision-making, where it can yield the most value.​.

    Humans decide what should be built, and check the finished product to determine whether it actually works and meets the established goals. Both the entry and exit points of the development process remain in the purview of trustworthy specialists, not just models.

    Sources indicate that of course, we also have to talk about an obvious problem here. If AI can write 10 times more code in the same time span as a human would manually, that means it can also produce 10 times more bad code. And AI cannot be trusted to simply check itself.​.

    Sources indicate that A method my own team uses is to separate code generation from code review. Like I already mentioned earlier, one model writes the code, and a model from a different vendor reviews. This is done to achieve a clean context. If the same model handles both, it’s less likely to scrutinize past decisions, because those already made sense to it when the code was originally generated.​.

    This is also why reviews should start with the original specifications, rather than the code itself. Looking for obvious mistakes and removing them is, naturally, a must. But the much more fundamental goal is to understand if the code actually matches with what you’re trying to build in the first place.​.

    Industry observers note that this changes how quality control works and at what stages it needs to happen. And as the use of AI-generated code becomes more commonplace, I think this change in approach will become increasingly necessary.

    As we covered at the start of this article, when AI becomes the fastest part of development, it can lead to latest problems.​.

    Code stops being the main bottleneck, and instead that bottleneck is born from everything that still requires in-person intervention from the human side of things. It can be a review, a customer decision, testing or something else. In my own practice, one of the most common statuses for a task these days is: “Merged, waiting for device testing.”​.

    That gives us a notion of how the development environment is changing around us. The real challenge now is not simply producing software faster; it’s how quickly we can go from an idea to a tested product that’s fully ready for release. And I think companies need to start paying more attention to measuring this difference.​.

    Sources indicate that the full impact of AI on the development process goes beyond just looking at how many more lines of code we can now write in the same amount of time. We also need to look at how many defects get discovered after a merge, and the amount of rework required as a result. And, of course, how long the queue of features is that are merged but still waiting for verification.​.

    These, to my mind, are much better signals of whether AI is actually making your business faster, and by how much.​.

    Industry observers note that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Sources indicate that after going public through an initial public offering (IPO) in June, SpaceX shares initially soared before falling back to earth. Right now, the stock is down 31% from highs, even though revenue grew well north of 100% year-over-year last quarter. Does that make the stock a promising opportunity right now?

    If you are thinking about buying the dip on SpaceX stock, here are three things you need to know before adding it to your portfolio.

    SpaceX was made famous by its awe-inspiring commercial rocket rolls out, including recent tests of the massive Starship rocket.

    Connectivity revenue grew to $5.25 billion last quarter, up 70% year-over-year. Importantly, these satellite internet services are highly profitable, generating $2.37 billion in operating income last quarter alone.

    There is still good runway for growth in Starlink's core customer base in rural areas, as well as in commercial services for boats and airplanes. However, in the long term, SpaceX has much grander ambitions to disrupt the entire telecommunications sector with direct-to-device internet capabilities worldwide. It will take many innovations to get there, but that is the thesis you are buying today: that Starlink can reach hundreds of billions in revenue a decade from now.

    In the immediate term, a bet on SpaceX is a bet on the company's aggressive ambitions to pivot to AI infrastructure investments.

    After acquiring Musk's xAI start-up in February 2026, SpaceX has begun building massive data centers to sell as an AI neocloud. This year, it has signed large deals with the likes of Anthropic and Alphabet, among smaller players. AI revenue was up to $7.56 billion last quarter, or more than 9x from a year ago.

    SpaceX expects even more rapid growth in the quarters ahead. It spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure capital expenditures last quarter. Overall tech giant capex is expected to double in the fourth quarter. By the end of next year, Musk forecasts overall annual recurring revenue (ARR) will reach $500 billion or higher. To be clear, that $500 billion is not a typo, but it also sits well above independent revenue estimates.

    On quarterly revenue terms, that would mean $125 billion in Q4 2027 revenue compared to $7.56 billion today. This is what an investment in SpaceX shares is betting on today.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:41 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Forward growth is going to be massively important for buying SpaceX right now. Why?

    According to recent reports, because the stock trades at a massive premium to its trailing financials. Right now, SpaceX has a market cap of $1.9 trillion and will likely continue to take on debt and sell new shares of common stock, diluting shareholders.

    That gives it a trailing price-to-sales ratio (P/S) over 50. A P/S ratio over 50 makes it one of the most expensive stocks on the market, especially if you only include large-cap stocks.

    Sources indicate that this means an investor buying today needs to have supreme confidence in SpaceX's growth trajectory. Its valuation will decline quickly if connectivity and AI revenue continue to grow at this rapid pace, but these are optimistic assumptions that Musk and the business are putting out there. A lot can go wrong when executing on a product vision.

    Unless you have high confidence that SpaceX can rapidly grow to hundreds of billions in revenue, the stock is probably one you want to avoid today.

    But is the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF a good investment for the future? Let's look at past historical returns data to see how rapidly this exchange-traded fund (ETF) could double your money if you invest today.

    It has been revealed that the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF only holds 102 stocks, but they tend to be good ones.     📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1039 w)
