    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    ​How Logistics Leaders Can Get Ready To Work Alongside AI Agents

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Philip Ellis is a founding frontend engineer at chrt, where he builds software for time-critical logistics operations.
    • Recent findings suggest that ​Most logistics teams have more data than they know what to do with.
    • In a recent development, that’s where AI agents can add value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Philip Ellis is a founding frontend engineer at chrt, where he builds software for time-critical logistics operations.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Most logistics teams have more data than they know what to do with. Every hour, they see telematics data, scan data, photos of proof of delivery, fuel data, invoices and exception emails. Often, they don’t have time to go through all of this, decipher what’s vital and act before a minor issue could escalate into a claim, chargeback or lost customer.​.

    In a recent development, that’s where AI agents can add value. A dashboard may sit unused until someone opens it, but an agent can sift through a flow of events, compare it to what should have happened and then take a specific action.

    Many logistics leaders are already exploring using agents in their operations, with 76% of surveyed chief supply chain officers saying that agentic AI will improve process efficiency in their organizations, according to an IBM report.

    However, as the founding front-end engineer of a organization that builds agentic technology for the logistics industry, I’ve found that many leaders are focused on the technology itself when they first have to understand where agentic AI can fit into their process and what’s required for successful implementation. ​.

    According to recent reports, good early agent uses involve clear rules, high volume and a high cost when something gets missed. In logistics, here are four possible areas that meet those criteria:.

    An agent can check a route against the blueprint, pick up a long stop or a deviation and then decide whether the delay would affect an appointment time. It can then pass relevant information on to the right person.

    Rather than looking at a map full of dots, a dispatcher could then pick up a short list of problems from that route.​.

    In a recent development, often, logistics fraud is subtle. Maybe an invoice is for more than it should be, or a pickup is made up. Maybe cargo is diverted or someone tries to trick the system when booking.

    Taken one at a time, each of these may look perfectly normal. But patterns start to emerge after hundreds of such records. An agent can, for example, look at documents, time stamps, location data and billing. It can also highlight inconsistencies and pass them on to someone to investigate. ​.

    Recent findings suggest that most audits are of a sample of transactions and take place after the fact. But an agent can monitor each transaction as it happens, check rates against a contract, confirm that there were relevant documents and identify discrepancies while they can still be corrected.

    In this way, an audit can become a regular daily activity rather than something done once a quarter.​.

    Recent findings suggest that every operation has standard operating procedures (SOPs), but there is often a gap between those procedures and what actually happens on the ground. ​.

    An agent can show you gaps in your procedures. And more importantly, it can show when your records don’t match reality.​ For instance, an agent can check each element of a procedure (e.g., temperature check, photo, seal check). In cases where it wasn’t done, the agent can trigger the necessary procedure. ​.

    An agent’s trustworthiness depends on the quality of the evidence it’s provided. If in your records you write what the proposal is, but nothing about what happened, the agent will quickly draw incorrect conclusions.

    And if connectivity fails in a trailer, in a yard or along a rural corridor, the agent could misread silence as compliance or silence as failure.​.

    Before relying on agents, leaders should ask three questions.​.

    • Can you trust the signal? Do you know where your records are incomplete, missing or estimated? And do you make that clear to the agent, rather than obscure it?

    • Do you record events or intentions?​ Are planned times, scans and confirmations the same as actual times, scans and confirmations? (They shouldn’t be.)​.

    • Does every process have an owner? When an agent sees a problem, it needs either a person or a rule to act on it. You don’t want a lights-out process. Instead, you want better use of people and of agents. ​.

    Agents can give relentless and repetitive attention to something, but people still bring judgment and the ability to think through the exceptions to rules.​​.

    According to recent reports, this leads to important considerations about decision rights. What should an agent be allowed to do on its own, such as raise a ticket or send a reminder? What needs approval, like payment of an invoice or action on a driver problem?

    Perhaps most importantly, does every action by the agent record what it saw, what it did and why? If you can’t explain an agent’s actions to a driver, regulator or customer, then it is inherently overstepping.​.

    Industry observers note that drivers, in particular, will rightly resist surveillance of their work. But used well, an agent can identify safety risks earlier, confirm the driver followed an SOP or confirm delays beyond the driver’s control. To get buy-in, explain what the agent is doing and why. Then, drivers may well see value in it as their records and jobs improve.​.

    In a recent development, once you have the process and oversight in place, take a specific, small problem in your business. Is an SOP step being followed? Are you coming across invoices that have already been sent? Start with the agent in “recommendation” mode. Let people compare what it suggests with their own view.​.

    According to recent reports, equally crucial: Watch for false alarms from the agent. Over time, too many could undermine value in a system. When trust develops and accuracy improves, gradually expand the authority and scope of agents.​.

    Most of the value from agents will flow to companies that provide them with reliable data, set limits for them and think of them as teammates in need of oversight. Historically, value in logistics has accrued to companies that spotted problems before others. Agents give more people the chance to spot problems sooner.​.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:15AM EST.

    According to recent reports, 10 stocks we like better than AGNC Investment Corp. ›.

    AGNC Investment (AGNC -0.53%) is a mortgage real estate investment trust (REIT). The stock's dividend yield is a shockingly high 17% as of this writing. But if you look at the dividend history, you come away with a clear message: You can't rely on the dividend if you are using it to pay for your living expenses. So, despite the yield, AGNC isn't a buy for income-focused investors in November or, frankly, any other month of the year. But total return investors may still want to take a look.

    According to recent reports, all the information you need to explain why AGNC isn't a reliable dividend stock is contained in a single chart. Note in the graph below that the dividend (the orange line) has been highly volatile and has generally trended lower for more than a decade. Worse, the stock price (the purple line) tends to follow the dividend. So, if you bought a decade ago, you'd have less income and less capital. That's a terrible outcome for a dividend investor trying to live off of their dividends.

    But what about that blue line? That's total return, which assumes dividend reinvestment. Although the recent rise in interest rates has pushed AGNC's stock price lower, reducing its total return, the long-term picture remains quite positive. Over time, AGNC has created value for investors that focus on total return. Based on the stock's history, it is a solid choice for total-return-focused investors seeking to diversify their portfolios by adding mortgage exposure into the mix.

    Recent findings suggest that but is November the time to buy AGNC? That's a harder question to answer because of the uncertainty around interest rates. The recent stock drop highlights the fact that rising rates can lead to a falling stock price. If rates continue to rise, the stock could continue to fall. However, that also increases the dividend yield, meaning that every time the dividend is reinvested, it buys more shares.

    AGNC isn't an easy investment to understand, and the lofty yield is only part of the story. If you are a long-term investor who is focused on total return and diversification, buying AGNC in November could be a reasonable decision. Just go in knowing the price is likely to be volatile until the interest rate environment stabilizes. If you can't handle that kind of uncertainty, then you probably shouldn't buy the stock right now.

    The five-star analyst mentioned that the meetings increased his confidence about CrowdStrike being an "crucial, well-positioned cybersecurity platform vendor that is an AI beneficiary given its expansive portfolio, unique data set, and ability to both secure AI and use AI to improve security.".

    Among the key takeaways, Borg noted that AI is driving a major shift in cybersecurity demand as it presents software vulnerabilities that can be exploited by less sophisticated hackers with capabilities that were once limited to government-backed hacking groups. This has led to companies making cybersecurity a top priority, driving customer interest in CrowdStrike's fresh AI Detection & Response solution and its broader security platform.

    Borg added that AI-driven demand is expanding CrowdStrike's pipeline and supporting confidence in the manufacturer's higher fiscal 2027 net latest annual recurring revenue guidance issued last quarter.     ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

    📅 05 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4134 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.
    • Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.
    • The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

    Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

    The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

    Industry observers note that but that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he noted.

    Recent findings suggest that “We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

    It has been revealed that “All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”.

    Recent findings suggest that despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he mentioned: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”.

    Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

    The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

    According to recent reports, raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

    It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

    But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

    It has been revealed that only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

    Recent findings suggest that “We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”.

    In a recent development, kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

    He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

    Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

    It has been revealed that if Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a major role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

    In a recent development, louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

    Sources indicate that the fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”.

    🌴 @RealBetis_en's Hector Bellerin reacts to a 3-1 preseason win over his former club Arsenal"I spent 10 years over there always trying to help and see Arsenal where it belongs, and it's nice to finally face them with them being in that position" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/er3YtAysQb.

    According to recent reports, “It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

    “All of us, together, we share a common goal. We have confidence to build on. We will take every game as it comes. The atmosphere was amazing. I did not realise Ireland has so many Arsenal fans. We are so grateful for everyone who came to support us today. We wanted to give them a good result and performance. Hopefully next time we can.”.

    In a recent development, “We always want to win and in the end we could not today. In some ways they deserved it and we could have done better. We did have some good moments though. We had an amazing season last season. I believe in this team and there are still players to come back from the World Cup. I am confident but we can always do better.”.

Isco attempts an audacious flick rather than putting his foot through it and his effort is saved by Meslier. That should have been a goal.

    Arsenal have changed nearly their entire starting XI whereas Betis have made just the one substitution thus far. Betis have played more games so far in pre-season, which probably explains the difference in the number of changes.

    You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

    Play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

    Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

    Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

    “When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

    In a recent development, “If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”.

    Recent findings suggest that premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the fresh season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

    Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    It has been revealed that real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

    They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that could a bear market be around the corner, happening this year or next?
    • According to recent reports, data source: Slickcharts.com, as of Nov.
    • In a recent development, with six of the past seven full years featuring double-digit gains, a pullback in the near future would not be surprising.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Selena Maranjian – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:27AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Sources indicate that could a bear market be around the corner, happening this year or next? Absolutely -- because stock market crashes and corrections, and, often, ensuing recessions, simply do happen every few years. Arguably, Wall Street is due for one. Check out the recent returns of the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%) index of America's 500 largest companies:.

    According to recent reports, data source: Slickcharts.com, as of Nov. 18, 2026. Returns reflect reinvested dividends.

    In a recent development, with six of the past seven full years featuring double-digit gains, a pullback in the near future would not be surprising. Other indicators, such as the Buffett indicator and the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, also favor a bear market of some sort.

    According to recent reports, the first way to prepare for a bear market is simply to expect it -- and to understand that it's extremely likely to end and be followed, eventually, by a market recovery. Check out some data from The Hartford Funds:.

    All that stated, there are different ways for different people to prepare for a bear market.

    Sources indicate that for older folks who may be living on a fixed income or will soon be getting by without a regular salary, it's probably best to be cautious. It's true that many bear markets end by the time your car needs its next oil change, but some can last several years. So to be on the safe side, don't keep any money that you expect to need within the next five years (or 10, to be more conservative) in the stock market. You don't want to have to sell to generate living expenses when your portfolio is temporarily smaller.

    You might put your short-term money in less volatile places, such as certificates of deposit (CDs), money market accounts, bonds, or high-yield savings accounts. Then you can draw on those investments as needed for living expenses.

    Sources indicate that if you're still young -- or youngish -- you can view market downturns more opportunistically. Like older folks, don't keep any short-term money in the stock market. You don't want to have to sell at a suboptimal time to generate, say, a down payment for a home or college tuition for your kid.

    As you anticipate a coming bear market, you might also try to stockpile some dollars -- as you look forward to a market pullback. Yes, it will hurt to see a portfolio worth, say, $400,000 become one worth, say, $300,000 or even $250,000 (for a while), but when most or all of your holdings are suddenly at depressed prices, the stocks of lots of great companies will be too. It's a terrific time to go shopping!

    Warren Buffett explained it all well in his 1997 letter to shareholders:.

    If you expect to be a net saver during the next five years, should you hope for a higher or lower stock market during that period? Many investors get this one wrong. Even though they are going to be net buyers of stocks for many years to come, they are elated when stock prices rise and depressed when they fall. [...] This reaction makes no sense. Only those who will be sellers of equities in the near future should be happy at seeing stocks rise. Prospective purchasers should much prefer sinking prices.

    Sources indicate that another way to prepare for a bear market -- whatever your age -- is to have a good emergency fund. It should be able to support you for at least three to six months, even if you lose your job. Job losses can happen more often in bear markets and recessions, after all.

    According to recent reports, consider holding some defensive stocks in your portfolio to balance any growth stocks. Defensive companies are ones whose offerings are needed regardless of the economic condition. Think shampoos, utilities, food, and so on. Know that when the market pulls back, high-flying growth stocks often fall harder.

    So don't worry too much about the possibility of a stock market crash. Instead, just prepare for one.

    #39060. Tech Report: How To Tell In Week Two Whether An AI Pilot Will Survive

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (936 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: How To Tell In Week Two Whether An AI Pilot Will Survive

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vivek Thomas, Founder & CEO of AISensum, building AI teammates that help store managers and frontline teams make better decisions every day.
    • Recent findings suggest that ​A few weeks ago, I looked at a retail pilot that was working perfectly.
    • Buyers report “adoption” as one blended number.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vivek Thomas, Founder & CEO of AISensum, building AI teammates that help store managers and frontline teams make better decisions every day.

    Recent findings suggest that ​A few weeks ago, I looked at a retail pilot that was working perfectly. The software scored every conversation, the reports arrived each morning, and the dashboards were green. Then someone checked the logins. For seven days, almost nobody in the stores had opened the app. Nobody had noticed, because every number we were watching described the technology. None of them described the people.

    Most AI pilots are judged this way. Vendors report accuracy and uptime. Buyers report “adoption” as one blended number. When the pilot stalls, both sides argue about whose fault it is, and the pilot is either extended out of politeness or killed for the wrong reason.

    In a recent development, after years of running pilots in stores, venues and offices, I now judge every pilot and every live project with three plain questions: Do people show up? Does the work score up? Does it pay off?

    Sources indicate that the first question is whether people follow the routine the technology depends on. This is discipline, and it is almost always the first thing to break.

    What discipline means changes with the use case. For a coaching tool, it means the cashier logs in, listens to their own conversations and does the practice. For a sales tool at the counter, it means the cashier actually makes the suggested offer to the guest, every time, including on a busy Saturday. For a decision tool, it means the manager opens the morning recommendations and either acts on them or writes down why not.

    According to recent reports, measure discipline as a funnel. Out of everyone who should be using the tool, how many logged in? How many completed each step? Most teams stop at the first line. The real story usually sits two steps further down.

    Sources indicate that the second question is whether the work itself is getting better. This is performance, and it is the result of the actions people take.

    Recent findings suggest that for a coaching tool, performance is whether people’s scores are good and rising. For a sales tool, it is the extra revenue from the offers that were made. For a decision tool, it is what happened after each decision was carried out.

    Industry observers note that discipline and performance must be measured separately. A team can follow every step and still score badly, which tells you the content or the model needs work. A team can score well while hardly using the tool, which tells you the habit has not formed and the results will fade.

    According to recent reports, the third question is whether the business is better off. This is impact, and it takes the longest to prove.

    • Consistency: Are improvements holding across people and across months, or do they depend on a few stars?

    • Business Result: Did store sales or margin move against similar stores without the tool?

    • Payback: Does the result pay for what the tool costs?

    Until a client shares sales data, impact stays marked as unknown, never as zero. An honest “not yet proven” protects both sides.

    Put discipline on the vertical axis and performance on the horizontal one, each scored from 0 to 100. Draw a line at 60 on both. Each pilot, or each store within a pilot, becomes one bubble, and the size of the bubble is its impact. See the figure here.

    The four zones tell you who has to act:.

    In a recent development, • Healthy (high discipline, high performance): People show up and the work is improving. The job now is to prove the payoff and grow the bubble.

    • Coach (high discipline, low performance): People are doing everything asked, but scores stay low. This one is on the provider: Improve the content, the model or the training.

    In a recent development, • Reengage (low discipline, high performance): The results are good where the tool is used, but the habit is weak. This one is on the client’s managers. A store manager who asks about the routine every morning fixes more than any software update.

    • At Risk (low discipline, low performance): Nobody is using it and nothing is improving. Act the same week, at the most senior level on both sides.

    Industry observers note that the map only works if someone looks at it every week. Review it in the same meeting, at the same time, with one named owner for every bubble outside the healthy zone.

    Recent findings suggest that it also gives you a clean rule for ending a pilot. If a pilot sits in the at-risk zone for two weeks and the client’s sponsor does nothing, end it. Weak technology can be fixed by the provider. A routine nobody enforces cannot be fixed from outside the building.

    This is also why I no longer accept “the technology works” as a status update. In the pilot I described, the technology did work. Within a week of putting discipline on the screen, the gap was visible to everyone, and the conversation moved from blame to a clear owner and a date.

    Technology is the part of a pilot a vendor controls. The habit belongs to the leaders who run the floor. Measure both, separately, every week, and most pilots will tell you how they end long before the final review.​.

    Industry observers note that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    In a recent development, for investors with $500 to spare, Bloom Energy (BE +6.41%) could present a buying opportunity. That is, if you're willing to stomach some volatility.

    According to recent reports, for starters, Bloom has become one of the hottest names in AI infrastructure, thanks to its fuel-cell systems, which let data centers generate electricity on-site rather than wait years to connect to a traditional grid. Given the uncertainty around AI spending, however, Bloom stock has been extraordinarily volatile, recently falling more than 40% from its all-time highs.

    So, with $500 to invest, is now the time to buy?

    NYSE · As of 9:36 AM ET 11/19/26.

    According to recent reports, there's no question that Bloom has blossomed enormously from the AI boom. Just look at its recent quarter: Third-quarter revenue surged 138% year over year to $1.24 billion, while operating income also jumped from just $7.8 million last year to $225 million.

    And with management anticipating as much as $4.6 billion in total revenue this year, Bloom has clearly entered a fresh phase of growth.

    Another bright spot from the third quarter: Bloom is becoming more profitable as its business expands. Its gross margin improved from about 29% a year ago to nearly 34% last quarter. It's never a bad thing when a organization keeps more of every dollar after accounting for production costs.

    In a recent development, so, business looks strong; it has never, in fact, looked stronger. Still, there are some less positive things to consider.

    Industry observers note that despite its knockout quarter, Bloom reported negative operating cash flow of $27 million, while also spending $153 million on capital expenditures. And while third-quarter revenue was soaring, a huge chunk of it (almost 70%) came from two contractual customers. That's an enormous amount of business concentrated in two hands.

    Sources indicate that one of those customers is Oracle (NYSE:ORCL), which agreed to buy as much as 2.8 gigawatts of power from Bloom for Oracle's data centers. And therein lies a risk with Bloom right now: The manufacturer could certainly survive a slowdown in data center spending, but its growth would likely take a serious hit. Worse, without extraordinary sales growth, Bloom's already lofty valuation would become harder to justify. Indeed, even after its brutal sell-off, the stock still trades for more than four times the S&P 500's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio.

    So, would I invest $500 in Bloom today?

    If I were a moderately aggressive investor willing to stomach substantial volatility, absolutely. The thing is, Bloom's technology addresses an electricity problem that extends beyond AI data centers. Even if AI spending slows, Bloom still has a market for its fuel cells, although one that might not support the extraordinary growth Wall Street has come to expect of it.

    That said, I wouldn't mistake the sell-off for a bargain. Bloom still has plenty to prove, and its valuation isn't cheap. But for investors with a long time horizon, $500 seems reasonable for a promising business whose best years could still lie ahead.

    La sfida è in programma il 22 dicembre alle 21 a San Siro; per i tagliandi sono previste prelazioni prima della vendita libera.

    According to recent reports, la Supercoppa Italiana 2026 si giocherà il 22 dicembre a San Siro: l’Inter affronterà la Lazio alle 21, ora locale. Secondo quanto riportato da Goal, Per acquistare i biglietti, i canali indicati sono Vivaticket e i portali dei club, con fasi di prelazione prima dell’eventuale vendita libera. I prezzi riportati sono invece stime, non tariffe ufficiali.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    La competizione torna alla formula a due squadre e si disputa nuovamente in Italia. L’Inter partecipa da campione in carica della Serie A; la Lazio è la finalista sconfitta dell’ultima Coppa Italia.

    I nerazzurri hanno preso parte alle ultime sei edizioni della Supercoppa, vincendo tre titoli consecutivi tra il 2021 e il 2023. L’ultimo successo biancoceleste risale al 2019. Lo scorso dicembre il trofeo è andato al Napoli, che ha battuto il Bologna 2-0 al King Saud University Stadium di Riad.

    L’Inter di Cristian Chivu giocherà nel proprio stadio e arriva alla sfida con una serie di dieci partite senza sconfitte contro la Lazio. Tra queste, Goal indica anche il 2-0 nella finale di Coppa Italia di maggio.

    I biglietti ufficiali per la Supercoppa sono venduti principalmente tramite Vivaticket, indicato come partner ufficiale della Serie A per la biglietteria, e attraverso i portali delle due società partecipanti.

    It has been revealed that la vendita gestita dai club per le gare di Supercoppa segue solitamente più fasi. Si comincia, settimane prima della partita, con la prelazione per gli abbonati. Seguono le fasi riservate ai titolari della tessera del tifoso o della CRN; se rimangono posti disponibili, si passa alla vendita libera.

    Per informazioni sui tagliandi, il riferimento indicato è costituito dai siti ufficiali dei club. La disponibilità sulle piattaforme di rivendita può essere consultata separatamente.

    • Sources indicate that sounds like a potentially great investment opportunity in artificial intelligence, right?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Johnny Rice – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:42AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Sources indicate that anthropic (ANT +0.00%) is set to start trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The IPO offering hopes to raise $81.3 billion publicly along with a $26 billion private placement for major tech investors. That makes it the biggest IPO of all time as measured by funds raised, and it will likely put the company’s valuation at $1.4 trillion.

    Sources indicate that sounds like a potentially great investment opportunity in artificial intelligence, right? The problem is, I don't see Anthropic having a real, lasting business advantage that keeps competitors from taking its AI customers. Among investment analysts, this is referred to as a durable moat, and it’s all-notable for long-term growth.

    It has been revealed that anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

    Right now, the company's main advantage is that its Claude AI models are consistently among the best available. Customers are clearly excited: Third-quarter revenue jumped 1,127% year over year -- incredible. But this is not a durable moat to me, and I am skeptical that the pace of growth will hold much longer.

    Sources indicate that over time, I think a lot of its customers will find that most of their AI needs can be met by models that aren't on the cutting edge, models that are good enough and can be attained for a fraction of the price. If that is the case, there's very little to keep these customers from leaving.

    Most of the company's lucrative enterprise clients use Claude through an application programming interface (API) -- basically a backend connection that lets a company's systems send work to Claude and get results back. That makes switching to another model provider pretty dang easy.

    Frankly, a customer doesn't even have to leave entirely. It could send the routine work to a cheaper competitor and keep Claude reserved for the hardest jobs. The question is, will there be enough of these "hardest jobs" to keep the revenue line going up?

    It’s something long-term investors need to consider as Anthropic releases its IPO.

    Tech Report: If the Fed Raises Rates Again in December, Here's the 1 ETF I'm Buying Without Any Hesitation

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Select Sector SPDR Trust - State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF ›.
    • "There's no such thing as a sure thing.
    • Just three weeks away from the Fed's final meeting of 2026, CME FedWatch data indicates there's a 96.8% chance the central bank raises rates by 25 basis points to close out the year (and a 3.2% chance of a 50-basis-point hike).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Todd Shriber – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Select Sector SPDR Trust - State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF ›.

    "There's no such thing as a sure thing. That's why they call it gambling." is a famous quote often attributed to Neil Simon, but we're talking about investing here, not gambling. Even if gambling were the topic du jour, it'd be fair to say it's a "lock" that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December.

    Just three weeks away from the Fed's final meeting of 2026, CME FedWatch data indicates there's a 96.8% chance the central bank raises rates by 25 basis points to close out the year (and a 3.2% chance of a 50-basis-point hike). The rate-tightening might not stop there, as some members of the smart-money crowd see another hike coming sometime in the first quarter of 2027.

    Financial services stocks may be primed to start winning if interest rates rise again. Image source: Getty Images.

    According to recent reports, so with the Fed expected to remain hawkish over the next several months, it's a good time for investors to remember that not all assets respond to rate hikes the same way. For example, precious metals are viewed as vulnerable to rising rates because higher rates make bonds more attractive, diminishing the allure of gold and silver, which don't pay dividends or interest.

    It has been revealed that on the other hand, some sectors are known as rising-rate winners. Investors can tap into those trends with exchange-traded funds (ETFs) such as the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF -0.10%).

    This $54.1 billion ETF is home to many of the largest financial companies trading on domestic exchanges and, ahead of its 28th birthday on Dec. 16, it's the oldest and largest ETF in the financial services category.

    Superlatives aside, let's quickly address a couple of important points. First, this SPDR ETF isn't dedicated to bank stocks. Second, although Treasury yields have climbed this year and the Fed has already hiked rates once, this SPDR ETF is up just 7.5% this year, trailing the S&P 500 by nearly 200 basis points.

    According to recent reports, perhaps it's time for this fund and its peers to start living up to their history of winning when rates rise. Usually, when longer-term rates creep higher, banks benefit because they raise the rates they charge to borrowers. This is a historical statistic, but financials are tied with technology as the second-best-performing sector a year following the first rate hike in a tightening cycle, trailing only energy.

    NYSEMKT · As of 9:39 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Banks aren't the only beneficiaries of rising rates. Insurance providers often benefit from that scenario, too. All that cash we consumers dole out to companies every month for car, home, or renters insurance is invested by those carriers, but the thing is, insurance companies usually invest that capital in ultra-safe assets, such as Treasuries. With a massive influx of cash from policyholders every month, insurance providers can buy upcoming bonds with higher coupon payments as rates rise. That's something to consider regarding this SPDR ETF, as it allocates nearly 14% of its portfolio to insurance stocks, and that does NOT include nearly 13% weight to Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -1.29%) (BRKB -1.03%), a manufacturer with significant insurance interests.

    Industry observers note that there's no sugarcoating it: the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF has been a dud at a time when the interest-rate environment is incredibly inviting for financial stocks. That remarked, history is still appealing here because it confirms this sector typically delivers impressive earnings growth as Treasury yields trend higher.

    Second, equity income investors shouldn't be put off by this ETF's 1.3% 30-day SEC yield. Yes, that's very light compared to 10-year Treasuries, but there's more to the story. Some Dividend Kings, companies with payout increase streaks of at least 50 years, reside in this ETF. That group includes S&P Global.

    On a related note, after a few years in "dividend purgatory" following the global financial crisis, significant bank dividends are on the mend, suggesting that long-term investors may be able to rely on this ETF for solid dividend growth regardless of what rates do.

    AI Is Getting Cheaper, Business Models Need To Catch Up

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tim Lee is the Founder and CEO of Bookipi, an international SaaS organization trusted by millions of small businesses worldwide.
    • A sharp correction in Chinese technology stocks recently caught my attention, but not because I think it predicts what will happen to AI stocks elsewhere.
    • Sources indicate that reuters reported that China’s STAR50 technology index fell 40% in less than four months, erasing about US$480 billion in market value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tim Lee is the Founder and CEO of Bookipi, an international SaaS organization trusted by millions of small businesses worldwide.

    A sharp correction in Chinese technology stocks recently caught my attention, but not because I think it predicts what will happen to AI stocks elsewhere.

    Sources indicate that reuters reported that China’s STAR50 technology index fell 40% in less than four months, erasing about US$480 billion in market value. The interesting part for business leaders is not the market movement itself but the tension underneath it: huge amounts of capital invested in AI while the technology itself becomes increasingly competitive.

    That tension is starting to change how I think about building with AI.

    In my work deploying AI into software products and internal workflows, I have become less interested in which model is considered the best and more interested in the economics of completing a task reliably.

    Industry observers note that that sounds like a small distinction. I think it will become an crucial one.

    Sources indicate that stanford’s “2026 AI Index Report“ demonstrates how rapidly the competitive landscape is tightening. The performance gap between leading models has narrowed considerably, including between leading U.S. and Chinese models. Stanford notes that this is shifting competition toward factors such as cost, reliability and domain-specific performance.

    This reflects what I see when we build AI workflows.

    For a business task, the question is rarely: Which model scored highest on a benchmark?

    The questions are more practical. Did it complete the task correctly? How often did a person need to intervene? How long did it take? What did a successful completion cost?

    It has been revealed that for example, an expensive model may perform slightly better on a benchmark but be unnecessary for a simple classification or extraction task. A smaller model may complete that task reliably at a lower cost. The more complex model can then be reserved for jobs where its additional capability creates measurable value.

    This makes model selection an operating decision rather than a technology preference.

    One lesson I have learned from deploying AI is that increasing usage does not automatically mean the product is improving.

    Every AI action can carry a variable cost. If usage doubles but revenue, retention or productivity does not improve with it, the business may simply be spending more money.

    This is different from much of traditional SaaS, where serving another interaction can have a very small marginal cost.

    The 2026 Stanford AI Index captures the scale of this challenge. AI organization revenue is growing rapidly, but compute costs and infrastructure investment are also reaching record levels. Global corporate AI investment more than doubled in 2025.

    For operators, that makes unit economics important much earlier in the product development cycle.

    When I look at an AI workflow now, I want to understand the cost per successful outcome rather than simply the number of prompts, conversations or agent actions.

    Sources indicate that if an agent processes 10,000 tasks, I want to know how many were completed correctly, how many required human assistance and what the total cost was. Then I want to compare that with the value created.

    That is a more useful measure of adoption.

    There is another side to these economics.

    If the cost of intelligence continues to decline while capability improves, many AI use cases that do not make economic sense today may become viable.

    This can benefit the companies applying AI rather than only those developing the underlying models.

    A customer support workflow that is too expensive to automate today may work at half the inference cost. An agent that is economical for enterprise customers may eventually work for a small business. A process that right now requires one employee to supervise 10 AI tasks may improve until that employee can supervise hundreds.

    This is where I see significant opportunity.

    Industry observers note that businesses do not necessarily need to own the foundational technology. They need to understand where cheaper intelligence can improve a workflow they already know well.

    Customer relationships, proprietary context, distribution and deep understanding of a workflow can remain valuable even as the models underneath a product change.

    For leaders evaluating AI investments, I would focus on a few operating questions.

    What business outcome is the AI responsible for? What does a successful outcome cost? How often does a human need to intervene? Does the customer keep using the capability after trying it? And do the economics improve as usage grows?

    Those answers matter more to me than how many AI features have been rolled out.

    In a recent development, the recent correction in China is a useful reminder of the difference between technological value and economic value. AI can become extraordinarily useful while individual companies struggle to capture enough of that value to justify their costs or valuations.

    For businesses adopting AI, that may actually be good news.

    More competition between models can mean better capability, lower prices and more choice. The opportunity for business leaders is to turn those improvements into workflows that customers repeatedly value at economics that make sense.

    That is where I would expect durable AI businesses to be built.​.

    According to recent reports, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    #39040. Anthropic Just Priced the Biggest IPO on Record. History Indicates What Record-Setting IPOs Have Meant for the S&P 500.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (830 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic Just Priced the Biggest IPO on Record. History Indicates What Record-Setting IPOs Have Meant for the S&P 500.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic (ANT +0.00%) priced its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday at $83 a share, selling 980 million shares, mostly upcoming stock from the company itself.
    • Recent findings suggest that it's the biggest IPO on record, if deals are compared before their extra shares.
    • Industry observers note that so I'll measure every deal here by its base deal, the shares sold before any of those extra purchases.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 19, 2026 at 8:53AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +0.00%) priced its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday at $83 a share, selling 980 million shares, mostly upcoming stock from the company itself. The price topped the $70-to-$78 range the company had expected, and it takes the amount raised to around $81.3 billion. Its shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, Nov. 19.

    Recent findings suggest that it's the biggest IPO on record, if deals are compared before their extra shares. SpaceX (SPCX +1.88%) raised $75 billion in its base deal in June, then around $86.3 billion overall after its underwriters bought more shares.

    Industry observers note that so I'll measure every deal here by its base deal, the shares sold before any of those extra purchases. (If Anthropic's underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares they have an option on, its total would reach around $93.5 billion, above SpaceX's on that basis, too.).

    Sources indicate that the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%) heads into the listing around 6% under its Oct. 6 record close of 7,818.93, after ending Wednesday at 7,323.63. How has the index done over the year after past record-setting IPOs?

    Five U.S. IPOs set the size record on this basis between 1999 and 2014, each one topping the last. United Parcel Service raised around $5.5 billion in November 1999. AT&T Wireless, which traded as a tracking stock, almost doubled that with around $10.6 billion in April 2000. Visa raised around $17.9 billion in March 2008, and Alibaba raised about $21.8 billion in September 2014.

    According to recent reports, general Motors sold around $15.8 billion of common stock in its November 2010 IPO, short of Visa's deal. But it sold around $4.35 billion of preferred stock at the same time. Including both, as the deal was widely reported, it was around $20.1 billion and set the record.

    It has been revealed that to measure what followed, I compared the S&P 500's close on each stock's first trading day to its close a year later. If the anniversary landed on a weekend, I used the previous trading day. These are price changes only, without dividends.

    The numbers aren't encouraging.

    Recent findings suggest that A year after UPS's debut, the S&P 500 was down under 1%. After AT&T Wireless, it was down around 14%.

    Sources indicate that the year after Visa's listing was much worse, with the index down about 40% as the financial crisis deepened. The only gain came after GM's debut, when the index climbed around 2%. And it dropped about 3% in the year after Alibaba's.

    An ordinary year has been much better. By my count from daily closes, the S&P 500 has been up 12 months later around three-quarters of the time since 1950, and the typical 12-month change has been a rise of about 11%.

    Industry observers note that notably, the index wasn't standing still along the way. In four of the five years, it rose around 6% or more above its starting level at one point (as much as 14% after GM's debut) before losing most or all of that ground.

    I don't think the IPOs themselves were to blame. The two major drops came in the dot-com bust and the 2008 financial crisis, and Visa listed with the S&P 500 already around 17% under its October 2007 record.

    It's tough to see how one share sale, however large, could trigger a bear market.

    Sources indicate that but the timing arguably isn't random, either. Companies and their early owners tend to sell the most stock when buyers are willing to pay the most for it. UPS listed a few months before the index's March 2000 peak, AT&T Wireless a month after it, and Alibaba a day after a record close.

    Put another way, I think a record-setting deal can be a sign that stock prices are already high, which could leave less room for a strong year afterward.

    Recent findings suggest that spaceX's record hasn't settled anything yet. From its June 12 debut, the S&P 500 rose to its Oct. 6 record, around 5% higher. It's now a bit more than 1% under where it began.

    Of course, five finished cases are way too few to trade on. I wouldn't sell an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF over Anthropic's listing -- I'd keep adding to one in regular amounts over time. But I'd keep my expectations for the coming 12 months modest.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:00AM EST.
    • Social Security benefits are slated to increase by 3.6% in January, thanks to the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA).
    • Here's a closer look at how you can estimate your 2027 Social Security benefit, how it compares to the average, and what to do if you don't think your checks will go far enough.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:00AM EST.

    Social Security benefits are slated to increase by 3.6% in January, thanks to the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA). This will add roughly $75 per month to the average check. But COLAs are percentages, so you could get more or less than this, depending on how your current benefit stacks up to the average.

    Here's a closer look at how you can estimate your 2027 Social Security benefit, how it compares to the average, and what to do if you don't think your checks will go far enough.

    Industry observers note that the typical senior claiming a Social Security retirement benefit in October 2026 received $2,092 per month. This is a record high, and with the COLA, the average check will surpass $2,100 for the first time in January. But not everyone will earn this much.

    Sources indicate that if your current Social Security checks are below the $2,092 average, you'll still get a benefit boost next year, but it'll be less than $75 per month. On the other hand, if you right now receive more than $2,092 per month, you'll receive an above-average boost.

    According to recent reports, you can get a rough idea of how much your checks will grow by adding 3.6% to your current benefit amount. But if you're on Medicare, keep in mind that rising Part B premiums will eat up some of this increase, so you may wind up with a little less than what you've calculated.

    The Social Security Administration will send out personalized COLA notices to all beneficiaries in early December. This will give you your exact benefit amount for next year, including Medicare Part B withholding if you're enrolled in this program.

    Once you know how much the Social Security COLA will add to your checks next year, you can start building your 2027 budget. Compare your fresh benefit amount to your average monthly retirement expenses to see how much you'll have to cover on your own.

    Then, work out a initiative for how you'll cover the rest. You might be able to make up the difference by withdrawing money from personal savings or relying on your paychecks, if you're still working. If those aren't options, you might have to look into full- or part-time employment or other government benefits to cover the difference. You could also use a combination of these strategies.

    #39036. Showing Up In AI Search Isn't The Same As Getting Recommended

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1028 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Showing Up In AI Search Isn't The Same As Getting Recommended

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Andrew Higgins is CEO of Parsnipp, an AI search marketing tech giant.
    • ​For the last 12 months, a lot of marketers have been diving into AI search marketing, and most have been defining success with a new KPI: “AI visibility.”.
    • AI visibility has been our primary measure of whether a brand is succeeding in AI search and appearing in LLM-generated answers related to its brand and market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andrew Higgins is CEO of Parsnipp, an AI search marketing tech giant.

    ​For the last 12 months, a lot of marketers have been diving into AI search marketing, and most have been defining success with a new KPI: “AI visibility.”.

    AI visibility has been our primary measure of whether a brand is succeeding in AI search and appearing in LLM-generated answers related to its brand and market. But what we’ve learned at Parsnipp is that visibility tells only part of the story. There’s a much larger conversation (pun intended) happening around how people interact with AI, and it’s one we need to start paying closer attention to.

    Recent findings suggest that when we started building in AI search, we measured what everyone measures: how often a brand reveals up in an AI answer. We tracked mentions, citations, share of voice, visibility scores, etc. A lot of this is derived from traditional search, and it’s the habit that’s trained into all of us. Win the keyword—or in this case prompt—and move on to the next.

    The more we tested and replicated the ways people actually use AI, the more it changed how I thought about the channel and what it means for brands.

    We wanted to see what happens after the first answer, because while most tools measure a set of prompts and AI responses for visibility, that’s not an accurate reflection of how real people use answer engines. So instead of firing single prompts at a model, my team simulated full shopper conversations: a person with a need, follow-up questions and constraints that come up along the way (i.e., the way people actually talk to LLMs).

    The scenario was simple: headphones under $150. We ran 320 conversations across ChatGPT and Gemini 3.8 Flash in two independent batches of 160 to check if the pattern held. What we found was that across 960 brand mentions, only 700 became an actual recommendation. Nearly three in 10 mentions went nowhere. This means what marketers considered a “win” was actually far from it.

    We had brands that scored incredibly well on visibility but almost never were the product or brand actually recommended by the end of the interaction with the shopper. On a visibility dashboard, that looks like a strong brand, but it was missing the last two-thirds of the shopper’s journey through AI.

    In traditional search, appearing in results was the first step in the customer journey. From there, our website and retail partners took over the consideration phase, helping customers compare products, read reviews, shop for the best price and, ultimately, make a purchase.​.

    It has been revealed that but in today’s world, with so much of that interaction taking place on one surface, between a shopper and their agent, AI now folds much more of this funnel into one channel. So, we’ve started thinking full funnel again, just inside the AI Search experience:.

    • Mentioned: The assistant brings you up.

    • Considered: You stay on the shortlist as the shopper adds needs.

    • Recommended: You’re the pick, not the runner-up.

    • Chosen: The shopper, or their agent, buys.

    Each stage leaks for a different reason, and most brands are only measuring the first one.

    In a recent development, you don’t need special software for a first pass. Here’s the process I’d hand any marketing team:.

    1. Start With One Category Of Prompts: Pick the one that drives the most revenue, and don’t try to map everything at once. Maybe it’s your competitive prompts, broad industry prompts, etc. ​.

    According to recent reports, 2. Write Briefs, Not Keywords: List 20 to 30 real buying situations with the constraints included. “Running shoes” are keywords whereas “moderately frequent runner with wide feet that is over 35” is a brief.​.

    Recent findings suggest that 3. Script The Conversation: Simulate the conversation broadly, then add constraints one at a time (budget, use case, fit, deal breakers). I’d also switch around the order of questions, too. As an example, in our test, results shifted depending on whether the budget came first or last.​.

    In a recent development, 4. Run It More Than Once, On More Than One Model: Answers vary run to run as LLMs still have a fair bit of drift response to response. Running multiple batches is what told us our pattern was real.​.

    According to recent reports, 5. Log Two Numbers Per Brand: Start off simple. You don’ t need to track too many points along the journey at first. Even jumping from 1 (visibility) to 2 (visibility + mention) will make a huge impact. This means you’ll be measuring how often your brand is mentioned and how often it’s recommended. You can do it for your competitors too in the same research. Recommendations divided by mentions is your recommendation rate.​.

    6. Find Your Sweet Spot: Being both mentioned and recommended is the ideal position. If a brand is rarely mentioned but consistently recommended when it does come up, that’s primarily a discovery problem—and generally the easier one to fix. Neither position is ideal, but the more concerning scenario is a brand that’s frequently mentioned but rarely recommended. It creates the appearance of visibility without actually translating into preference or consideration.​.

    7. Identify What’s Holding You Back: Whether it’s price, product fit, a missing specification or a use case your brand doesn’t adequately address, identify the factors causing AI to steer customers elsewhere. These gaps are likely where you’re losing sales—and where your AI search marketing efforts should focus.

    Recent findings suggest that 8. Fix The Evidence, Then Re-Run: Make your product pages, reviews and third-party coverage answer that gap directly since LLMs have a tendency to repeat what they can find. Then test again next month because models change super fast.​.

    If your AI search report only counts mentions, it’s telling you half the story—and maybe the wrong half. Count the mentions, track the picks, fix the gap, and start thinking of AI search as a full funnel marketing channel instead of just a visibility goal.

    Recent findings suggest that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Here's why.

    As outlined in its Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, Anthropic has long-term spending commitments totaling $900.9 billion, with $451.6 billion expected to occur before the end of 2030.

    Under its "infrastructure service arrangements," Anthropic has significant commitments to buy AI compute and infrastructure services (including graphics processing unit, or GPU, compute demand) from Microsoft ($47.2 billion to $49.2 billion), Alphabet's Google (at least $121.3 billion), Amazon.com (at least $110 billion), and SpaceX for up to $120.5 billion "to access compute powered by NVIDIA GPUs.".

    The SpaceX deals are the most interesting and, by some distance, the most key for the company's AI strategy.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:37 AM ET 11/19/26.

    SpaceX CEO Elon Musk recently caused a stir by arguing that many neoclouds (cloud computing providers built solely for AI) would face extinction due to a lack of funding availability for companies that don't have revenue independent of AI. In the same X post, he noted that "SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.".

    Recent findings suggest that in other words, SpaceX is in a financial position to build out the infrastructure to meet demand from Anthropic and others, while many potential rivals are not. That financial strength partly relies on the expectation of future revenue from Anthropic. The Wall Street analyst consensus, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence, expects SpaceX to spend $770 billion on capital over the next three years. However, SpaceX needs AI enterprises, such as Anthropic, to commit to demand to justify this sort of AI infrastructure build-out.

    As such, the Anthropic IPO is positive for SpaceX for the following reasons:.

    Sources indicate that an additional reason needs circumspection, as it cuts both ways. While Anthropic has agreements committing $120.5 billion to SpaceX, each party can cancel agreements in "periods ending in January 2027 and March 2027 under the respective agreement; each agreement may be canceled" given 90 days' notice.

    It has been revealed that if you are bullish on AI-driven demand for GPU compute, you might think SpaceX could cancel the agreement and sell to other customers at higher prices. If you take a more bearish view on AI demand, you would be concerned that SpaceX is first in line if Anthropic needs to pare back spending or it develops its own data centers. The other agreements discussed above with Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are not cancelable unless there is a breach of contract.

    A successful Anthropic IPO strengthens the more optimistic case and, ultimately, the case for buying SpaceX stock.

    10 stocks we like better than Royal Caribbean Cruises ›.

    Certainly, no one can predict when a recession might come. Recently, many economists thought we'd have an economic slowdown in 2023 following the Federal Reserve's rate hikes the previous year.

    Sources indicate that while that never came to pass, we will have a recession at some point. We've already seen the market react negatively amid fears of how a technology spending slowdown will affect the overall economy.

    Investors can prepare themselves by buying and holding stocks of strong consumer goods companies through volatile periods, since these stocks can provide outsize gains over the long haul. That's because their short-term volatility gets smoothed out over time.

    These three stocks, with their strong market positions, offer this potential.

    According to recent reports, royal Caribbean Cruises (RCL -2.07%) is one of the most popular cruise line companies, commanding a high market share. Operating under the Royal Caribbean (family and premium segments), Celebrity (premium), and Silversea (ultra-luxury) brands, it generally targets a higher-income demographic.

    According to recent reports, their customers aren't immune from outside economic forces. People will undoubtedly cut back on expensive vacations if their personal finances significantly worsen. That would hurt short-term results, and the stock price is likely to decline.

    Still, Royal Caribbean remains a popular option, and demand will likely bounce back. You can see that from the current results.

    According to recent reports, its third-quarter load factor, a measure of occupancy, came in at 112%. Load factor is an industry benchmark that divides passenger cruise days by available passenger cruise days.

    NYSE · As of 9:41 AM ET 11/19/26.

    This helped drive quarterly revenue 9% higher year over year. Management expects the same growth throughout 2026. Bookings remain strong heading into 2027, with next year up by a high-teen percentage.

    Recent findings suggest that coca-Cola (KO -2.90%) belongs to the consumer staples segment. Theoretically, that means demand for its products shouldn't dip much during a recession. However, a significant portion of the manufacturer's revenue comes from outside the home (e.g., stadiums, movie theaters, and restaurants).

    According to recent reports, naturally, that would affect the tech giant's revenue. It's an extreme case, but stay-at-home orders during the early days of the pandemic significantly hurt Coca-Cola's product volume in the away-from-home market.

    But it bounced back when governments lifted restrictions, and it will likely do so again. Despite higher prices presently hurting consumers, they're still buying Coca-Cola products.

    You can see that in the manufacturer's sales. Most recently, Coca-Cola's third-quarter adjusted revenue grew 7% year over year. Higher volume primarily drove the increase.

    NYSE · As of 9:43 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Sources indicate that coca-Cola has also reliably increased dividends, an notable source of the stock's total return, which could help offset the stock price decline during difficult days. In fact, the firm has raised payments for 64 straight years. That makes the company a Dividend King, or one that has increased dividends for at least 50 consecutive years.

    Home Depot (HD -1.23%) has the highest sales among home-improvement retailers. With a ubiquitous presence and attractive prices, the retailer draws both do-it-yourself homeowners and professional contractors.

    Recent findings suggest that naturally, demand for its products and services fluctuates with the economy. That's because homeowners typically don't undertake major renovations when they have dim employment prospects. Homebuying, another source of projects, typically wanes during recessions.

    Recent findings suggest that currently, demand for major renovations has slipped as people pay more for everyday items. Additionally, home sales have dimmed as mortgage rates have jumped.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, despite these factors, Home Depot has posted positive same-store sales (comps). Its fiscal third-quarter comps grew 2.2%. The period ended on Nov. 1.

    NYSE · As of 9:41 AM ET 11/19/26.

    It has been revealed that shareholders can also confidently collect dividends, even during difficult days. Home Depot has raised payments every year since 2010. Even during the Great Recession, the organization kept dividends constant from 2007 through 2009.
