However, investors hoping for a quick rebound received some disappointing news: Nike doesn't expect to return to market-level revenue growth until fiscal 2029.

    According to recent reports, that lengthy recovery timeline raises an important question: How much should investors pay today for earnings that might not materialize for another five years? Here's the price I'd pay to buy more shares of Nike stock right now.

    Industry observers note that nike reiterated its fiscal 2027 outlook at its Investor Day and shared its 2031 framework with investors. The organization still anticipates that this fiscal year will be challenging. It expects a high-single-digit revenue decline and an even bigger drop in adjusted earnings, which it sees falling to a range of $1.15 to $1.35 per share. Meanwhile, the company expects to return around $2.4 billion to investors through dividends and share repurchases. That's down from the $2.5 billion it returned last year, which included $2.4 billion in dividends (a 5% increase) and $123 million in share repurchases.

    Recent findings suggest that however, its longer-term outlook is much brighter. Nike unveiled its full-stride-ahead strategy, which establishes a 2031 framework targeting $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from its fiscal 2027 baseline (for context, fiscal 2026 revenue was $46.4 billion). Additionally, it expects its operating margin to expand from 6% this fiscal year to 12%-14% by 2031, and adjusted earnings per share to rise from $3.00 to $3.50 by the end of fiscal 2031. If Nike can achieve that target, its earnings would more than double from 2027's expected level.

    NYSE · As of 9:43 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Additionally, the manufacturer expects to return a cumulative $12 billion in cash to shareholders through dividends during that time frame. That's about $2.4 billion annually, or equivalent to the current dividend. The company delivered its 24th consecutive dividend increase last November (up 3% per share). Its current guidance implies little to no dividend growth over the next five fiscal years as it focuses on investing to restore sustainable growth.

    It has been revealed that the biggest problem with Nike's outlook is that sales growth is still years away. The company expects fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 to be periods of investment in growth and in strengthening the quality of its business. It anticipates that its revenue will continue to decline in 2028, though the slump should moderate next year.

    It finally expects to return to market-level revenue growth by fiscal 2029. By fiscal 2030, revenue growth should reaccelerate and exceed market growth as its strategic investments begin to deliver results. That's a long time to wait for a reacceleration.

    According to recent reports, the longer the turnaround takes, the greater the risk that management's earnings targets slip or require additional investment. The firm's turnaround has already taken much longer than initially expected due to tariffs, competition, and other factors.

    Industry observers note that nike's ambitious earnings targets suggest its stock could deliver attractive returns over the next five years. However, the price investors pay today will play a major role in determining those returns.

    In a recent development, let's assume Nike achieves the midpoint of its fiscal 2031 adjusted earnings target of $3.25 per share. Applying a relatively conservative price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 16x would put its stock price at $52 in five years. Investors could also collect dividends along the way. Assuming Nike maintains its current annual dividend of $1.64 per share, shareholders would receive another $8.20 over five years. Combined, that implies an annualized total return of approximately 9.5% based on the shoe stock's recent share price near $38. That's a respectable potential return, but it leaves little room for the turnaround to disappoint.

    I'd prefer to buy Nike stock between $32 and $35 per share. At $35, the same assumptions imply an annualized return of approximately 11.5%, while a $32 purchase price would increase that potential return to about 13.5%.

    Sources indicate that nike's turnaround could eventually reward patient investors. However, given the lengthy recovery timeline and execution risks, I'd want a bigger margin of safety before buying.

    Prediction: A Stock Market Crash Is Coming. Here's What Investors Should Do Based on 100 Years of History.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that over the long haul, the U.S.
    • Much recent growth has been driven by a brand-upcoming industry called generative artificial intelligence (AI), which has seen America's tech giants pour billions into compute and memory hardware for data centers.
    • That said, equity prices don't go up every single year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Ebiefung – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:27AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Sources indicate that over the long haul, the U.S. stock market is a wealth-creating machine. And this is exemplified by the performance of the benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%), which has risen by a whopping 246% over the last decade. That represents a compound annual growth rate of 13.2%, noticeably above the index's historical average of 10%.

    Much recent growth has been driven by a brand-upcoming industry called generative artificial intelligence (AI), which has seen America's tech giants pour billions into compute and memory hardware for data centers.

    That said, equity prices don't go up every single year. And history highlights that periods of abnormally high growth usually end with drawdowns as excitement fades and Wall Street gets a more realistic view of what the future will bring. Let's explore some historical examples to help investors understand what comes next and figure out strategies to stay ahead.

    By now, you have probably heard that the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio is near record highs. This is a stock market valuation metric that compares the index's current prices to average inflation-adjusted earnings over the past 10 years. It smooths out the effects of short-term fluctuations, giving investors a clearer view of what the market is worth today compared with other periods in history.

    Over the last 100 years, the S&P 500's CAPE ratio has spiked three main times. The first was in late 1929, when it hit 32.6 right before the stock market crash that led to the Great Depression. The second time was during the dot-com bubble in late 1999, when it hit 44.2 (the index declined by 9.1% and 11.9% in the following two years).

    With a CAPE ratio of around 40, the third major spike is underway. And it is being driven by many of the same factors that sparked the dot-com bubble over two decades ago. Generative AI is promising to transform the way people live and do business. And Wall Street is pouring money into the opportunity, even though its long-term cash flow and profit-generating potential are far from established.

    Industry observers note that unlike the dot-com bubble, which was led by unprofitable internet stocks, the generative AI boom is dominated by some of the world's largest and most profitable technology companies. This includes names like Nvidia and Micron, which help supply the compute and memory chips hyperscalers use to run and train large language models (LLMs).

    These companies enjoy some level of safety due to their strong economic moats and high profits. These can be used to fund shareholder goodies like buybacks, which can support stock price growth. That noted, they aren't without their risks.

    In a recent development, research firm Gartner has joined a growing chorus of analysts getting nervous about the AI industry. They point to the alarming gap between what hyperscalers are spending on AI infrastructure and the actual revenue generated on the consumer side of the opportunity, and expect an eye-popping $3.5 trillion impairment charge as these assets are written down to better reflect their actual value-creating potential.

    Such a huge reversal in market optimism could have severe impacts on the S&P 500's performance, especially given that the top five tech giants now account for 30% of the index's total value.

    Over the long term, the S&P 500 has always bounced back from corrections and crashes. That means investors who already own the index shouldn't panic sell because of the recent uncertainty. That said, the market has become unusually exposed to the vulnerable AI industry, and it may make sense to boost diversification by allocating capital to other, less exposed industries.

    • Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a tech giant's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stock market continues to grapple with volatility amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Given this uncertainty, investors looking for steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a tech giant's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    In a recent development, downstream energy tech giant Phillips 66 (PSX) is this week's first dividend pick. With a quarterly dividend $1.27 per share (annualized dividend of $5.08), PSX offers a yield of 2.25%. The company recently reported solid Q2 earnings, as the Middle East conflict affected global supplies and drove up refining margins.

    Following the Q2 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Phillips 66 and raised his price target to $255 from $240, reflecting higher 2026 earnings expectations and lower interest expense next year.

    According to recent reports, gabelman highlighted the quarter-over-quarter reduction in Phillips 66's net debt, noting management's optimism at achieving its estimated $15.5 billion net debt target one year ahead of schedule. The 5-star analyst expects the firm to end 2026 with a net debt of $14.6 billion.

    "The [balance sheet] improvement could re-establish PSX as a go-to defensive refiner," noted Gabelman.

    Management agreed that PSX's payout ratio lagged year-to-date, but expects buybacks to increase in the second half. Gabelman said Phillps indicated the possibility of a larger dividend hike following an annual increase of 5% over the past two years.

    Gabelman ranks No. 554 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Phillips 66 Statistics on TipRanks.

    Crescent Energy (CRGY) is an exploration and production manufacturer with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Uinta Basins. Earlier this month, the company reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings and revealed a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, payable on August 31. At an annualized dividend of $0.48 per share, CRGY boasts a dividend yield of about 4%.

    In reaction to Q2 results, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reaffirmed a buy rating on Crescent Energy stock with a price target of $18. He noted continued strength in the company's performance, with second-quarter oil production and cash flow surpassing the Street's expectations.

    "CRGY's cash flow exceeded expectations by 10%, reinforcing its trajectory of capital efficiency," said Richardson.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that Crescent raised its full-year oil production guidance, citing the effective integration of the Vital Energy acquisition. Specifically, Crescent tripled its synergy target from the Vital Energy deal to as much as $300 million, significantly reducing the effective purchase price. This reflects Crescent's solid execution following the acquisition, Richardson noted.

    Additionally, the analyst noted that Crescent's capital spending is and heading toward the lower end of management's prior guidance, indicating disciplined financial controls.

    Sources indicate that richardson ranks No. 579 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.5%. See Crescent Energy Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Finally, Viper Energy (VNOM) is effectively controlled by Diamondback Energy. Viper owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests in oil-weighted basins, mainly the Permian in West Texas. Viper recently announced its Q2 2026 results and declared a 32% hike in its base dividend, effective in the third quarter of 2026. The new base dividend indicates a 4.5% annualized yield.

    Sources indicate that viper also removed its quarterly commitment to return at least 75% of cash available for distribution. The manufacturer believes that this move will ensure increased flexibility to make opportunistic share repurchases and pursue accretive mergers and acquisitions.

    Following the Q2 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper, slightly raising his price target to $59 from $58. Bilkoski remarked Viper's solid Q2 performance supports his view that the strength in oil prices and rising operator activity are driving higher production.

    Sources indicate that "Viper has delivered, and we forecast will continue to deliver, one of the highest production per share growth profiles in our royalty universe" through the end of 2027, said Bilkoski. He believes Viper deserves a premium valuation, given its above-average growth.

    It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst said that while the biggest surprise in the quarter was Viper's revision to its shareholder return framework, he doesn't believe that the move indicates a significant change to its underlying strategy. Under the new framework, a larger portion of excess free cash flow is expected to be allocated to share repurchases than to variable dividends, Bilkoski said.

    Industry observers note that bilkoski ranks No. 719 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Viper Energy Financials on TipRanks.

    Tech Report: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
    • Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.
    • Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    In a recent development, aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    Stepping up in the significant moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

    Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7.

    Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

    Recent findings suggest that the final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

    According to recent reports, victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i.

    The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

    It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

    There will be four added minutes.

    Sources indicate that when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

    Sources indicate that gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

    According to recent reports, for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

    In a recent development, maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

    Sources indicate that abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

    According to recent reports, boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

    Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

    Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

    Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

    A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

    Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

    Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

    Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

    Industry observers note that that is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

    It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

    Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

    Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

    According to recent reports, just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

    Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half.     Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

    Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

    It has been revealed that tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

    Recent findings suggest that bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

    The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

    There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

    Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

    The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

    That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

    According to recent reports, bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

    The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

    Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

    It has been a significant summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

    “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

    In a recent development, “It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that.     Recent findings suggest that aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

    After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

    Sources indicate that unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

    Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

    After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: 3 Critical-Mineral Stocks That Could Help You Make a Fortune by 2035

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, when governments call a mineral "critical" they're telling you two things: One, their economy depends on it, and two, they're worried about its supply.
    • In that light, three mining stocks -- Albemarle (ALB -0.75%), MP Materials (MP +3.74%), and USA Rare Earth (USAR +11.13%) -- could help patient investors build wealth by 2035.
    • Industry observers note that first up is Albemarle, a chemicals organization best known for producing lithium.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than MP Materials ›.

    According to recent reports, when governments call a mineral "critical" they're telling you two things: One, their economy depends on it, and two, they're worried about its supply. Both have been pushing governments and manufacturers alike to seek out more dependable sources. It follows, then, that companies that can meet that need could win some serious business -- and potentially generate substantial returns for investors as a result.

    In that light, three mining stocks -- Albemarle (ALB -0.75%), MP Materials (MP +3.74%), and USA Rare Earth (USAR +11.13%) -- could help patient investors build wealth by 2035.

    Industry observers note that first up is Albemarle, a chemicals organization best known for producing lithium. It is, in fact, one of the world's largest lithium producers, with activities that span mining, extracting lithium from brine, and processing it into chemicals used in rechargeable batteries.

    NYSE · As of 9:40 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Since lithium is on the U.S. government's critical-minerals list, securing a reliable supply is a national must-have, and few are as well equipped to meet that need as Albemarle. Indeed, the company itself expects global lithium demand to roughly double between 2025 and 2030, an outlook that aligns with the International Energy Agency's projection that lithium supply could fall short of demand by 2035.

    Albemarle already has mines and processing plants to help meet that demand, as well as ways to increase output. One way is to produce additional lithium through the expansion of its Australian mines; another is to extract more lithium from the brine it processes in Chile. Both give it a pretty credible path to a larger business by 2035, although, to be sure, its profits will depend heavily on lithium prices.

    MP Materials is at the forefront of a national effort to build a domestic supply chain for rare-earth elements, the group of 17 elements with a similar chemical makeup, including praseodymium, neodymium, and terbium, among others.

    Despite the name, many of these elements are relatively abundant in the Earth's crust. Finding deposits that can be mined profitably, however, isn't exactly common. In that sense, MP is one of the few companies in the U.S. with an operating rare-earth mine: Mountain Pass in California.

    NYSE · As of 9:43 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Industry observers note that obviously, extracting rare-earth elements from the ground is important, but what makes MP so interesting is its push to turn those materials into the kind of permanent magnet found in electric vehicles, robots, defense systems, personal electronics, and other technology. Since China dominates rare-earth processing and magnet manufacturing, MP could help U.S. manufacturers reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers.

    MP's planned 10X magnet plant, expected to begin commissioning in 2028, could bring MP's total magnet capacity to about 10,000 metric tons annually, giving it plenty of room to grow into a bigger business by 2035.

    Like MP, USA Rare Earth is trying to build a rare-earth supply chain in the U.S. Unlike MP, however, USA Rare Earth's U.S. mining project -- Round Top deposit in Texas -- is still being developed.

    Sources indicate that that mentioned, USA Rare Earth has spent the past year getting its ducks in a row. Last November, it bought Less Common Metals, a U.K.-based rare-earth metal producer, and more recently its acquisition of Serra Verde gave it an operating mine in Brazil. The Brazilian mine in particular is a source of dysprosium and terbium, two rare-earth elements that help magnets keep their strength at high temperatures.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:45 AM ET 11/19/26.

    According to recent reports, there's plenty of room for USA Rare Earth to grow. Its magnet factory in Stillwater, Oklahoma, made its first commercial magnet sales in September, and management is aiming to double the facility's annual magnet capacity by the second quarter of 2027. Meanwhile, the initial production from Serra Verde is covered by a roughly 15-year purchase agreement with a buyer backed by the U.S. government.

    If it can get Round Top up and running, USA Rare Earth could become a linchpin in America's rare-earth supply chain -- and help patient investors build substantial wealth by 2035.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Recent findings suggest that rocket Lab's (RKLB +4.39%) next significant opportunity hasn't left the launchpad, but customers are already lining up. The Space Exploration Technologies challenger has carved out a niche for itself in launching small payloads into orbit. Its next move is Neutron, a medium-lift rocket that could open a new high-margin revenue stream, with 16 flights planned through 2030.

    Sources indicate that if Neutron's flight schedule is filling up, why did Rocket Lab shares fall after earnings? The answer starts with the gap between booking a launch and delivering one.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:40 AM ET 11/19/26.

    Rocket Lab has emerged as the top space launch organization after SpaceX thanks to its Electron launch vehicle. This small-lift rocket has a payload capacity of roughly 300 kilograms (kg) to low Earth orbit, which pales in comparison to SpaceX's Falcon 9, which has a payload capacity of 22,800 kg. This massive difference gives Rocket Lab an advantage: It can provide dedicated introduces catered to customers' specific needs.

    Recent findings suggest that electron earns roughly $8 million to $10 million per launch. However, to better compete for larger contracts and improve profit margins, Rocket Lab has been developing its medium-lift Neutron launch vehicle, which can carry payloads over 40 times larger than Electron.

    At 13,000 kg, Neutron can enable human spaceflight, including cargo and crew resupply to space stations, and help it compete more effectively for contracts to deliver government or commercial satellite constellations into space. According to management, recent flights are commanding up to $70 million per launch and margins of 50% or more.

    Industry observers note that getting Neutron off the ground hasn't been smooth. On Jan. 21, the firm experienced a testing failure during a hydrostatic pressure test when one of its tanks ruptured, requiring management to refine its tank manufacturing process. Then in October, the company discovered tiny air pockets in the carbon-fiber composite of Neutron's forward dome.

    According to recent reports, as a result of these setbacks, the manufacturer has pushed back Neutron's launch timeline to 2027. Given the setbacks, CEO Peter Beck hasn't committed to a specific time period. Instead, the company wants to see its Stage 1 tank succeed in testing before committing to a given launch window.

    These setbacks have weighed on Rocket Lab's stock, which has fallen 64% from its 52-week high price of $151 per share.

    On top of this, Rocket Lab has a growing space systems business that helps complement its launch services. Here, the firm provides a wide range of services for engineering and manufacturing space components, including space solar cells, satellite trackers, ground command-and-control systems, on-orbit operations management, and satellites.

    As part of this growing business, on June 29, Rocket Lab unveiled it would acquire Iridium Communications, valuing the company at roughly $8 billion. To fund this acquisition, Rocket Lab issued 29 million fresh shares in September, adding further selling pressure on the stock.

    The acquisition gives Rocket Lab Iridium's global satellite communications network spectrum, including 66 active satellites, further expanding its end-to-end space stack.

    In a recent development, in the third quarter, Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron missions totaling $515 million, and the tech giant now has committed to 16 missions over the next several years. Because roughly half of its rolls out will be for its own satellite constellations, available commercial slots for Neutron are booked into the 2030s.

    According to CFO Adam Spice, the firm expects adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to turn positive about six months after Neutron's first successful flight, with positive free cash flow coming later.

    Rocket Lab continues to build on its end-to-end space business, and Neutron will be a substantial part of its future. For investors bullish on the long-term outlook for the space economy in the next decade and beyond, Rocket Lab is a top pure-play space stock to buy now.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    I’m Buying Anthropic Stock, Just Not on Day 1. Here’s My Strategy.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Matt Frankel, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:46AM EST.
    • It has been revealed that anthropic (ANT +0.00%), the tech giant behind the Claude AI models, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT.
    • I've called Anthropic arguably the most impressive pre-IPO company I've ever seen, and I plan to own it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Matt Frankel, CFP® – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:46AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    It has been revealed that anthropic (ANT +0.00%), the tech giant behind the Claude AI models, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq today under the ticker ANT. It's one of the most anticipated IPOs in history, and the final pricing showed just how much demand there is.

    I've called Anthropic arguably the most impressive pre-IPO company I've ever seen, and I plan to own it. But I'm not planning to buy shares the minute they start trading. Here's why, and how I plan to approach adding the AI giant to my portfolio.

    It has been revealed that to say that there was a lot of demand for Anthropic's IPO would be an understatement. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its original range of $70 to $78.

    In a recent development, it also increased the size of the deal by about 19%, selling 980 million shares, about 956 million from the manufacturer and the rest from its co-founders. At an $83 IPO price, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion. Including a separate $26 billion private placement, the total deal size is $107.3 billion, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion and making it the largest IPO on record, surpassing SpaceX (SPCX +1.60%).

    Speaking of SpaceX, that is easily the closest comparison. It was a similarly-sized IPO that priced at $135 in June and closed its first day at $160.95, up 19%. Just days later, it hit an intraday high of $225.64. Since then, it has fallen about 35% from that peak to around $145.

    Recent findings suggest that of course, there's no guarantee Anthropic stock follows the same path. For one thing, its public float is larger. SpaceX sold only about 4% of its shares, while Anthropic's 980 million shares are more than 7% of its total. Anthropic's lock-up also releases insider shares in stages, starting with up to 316 million on the first day of trading. More supply could mean a smaller pop, and possibly a smaller drop once the initial hype dies down. But the point is that nobody, myself included, has a crystal ball that can tell us whether Anthropic's stock will be higher or lower than its IPO price in a day, a week, a month, or a year.

    I plan to wait at least a few days for the excitement around these IPO stocks to settle before I buy anything. If the price has come back toward the IPO price, I'll open a normal starter position. If the hype has pushed it far above $83, I'll take a small nibble and build the position gradually.

    Either way, I'm thinking in years, not days. Anthropic's growth is remarkable, but it also faces enormous computing bills and stiff competition, so I want room to add if the stock gets cheaper. Having said that, I'd rather own a small piece of this business at a fair price than wait for a perfect price that may never come.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Dick's Sporting Goods ›.
    • According to recent reports, as physical stores stage a comeback against the digital wave, investors are weighing the stability of retail giants against specialized e-commerce platforms.
    • DICK'S Sporting Goods is a leading destination for athletes and sneaker fans, with a massive physical and digital footprint.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jake Lerch – Nov 19, 2026 at 9:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dick's Sporting Goods ›.

    According to recent reports, as physical stores stage a comeback against the digital wave, investors are weighing the stability of retail giants against specialized e-commerce platforms. Choosing between DICK'S Sporting Goods (DKS -3.20%) and Etsy (ETSY -0.48%) requires evaluating two distinct growth paths.

    DICK'S Sporting Goods is a leading destination for athletes and sneaker fans, with a massive physical and digital footprint. In contrast, Etsy operates a global marketplace for unique, creative goods, connecting millions of independent entrepreneurs with buyers. This comparison highlights the difference between a traditional retail powerhouse and a high-margin digital platform.

    In a recent development, DICK'S Sporting Goods focuses on being an omnichannel leader among retail stocks by offering apparel, footwear, and equipment through its namesake stores and expanding banners such as Foot Locker. The firm serves a wide range of athletes and sneaker enthusiasts across North America, Europe, and Asia, aiming to provide a premium shopping experience both in-store and online. A significant partnership with Nike (NKE -2.01%) accounts for nearly 31% of merchandise purchases, and customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $21.1 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 53.5% over the previous 12-month period. This significant expansion helped the tech giant achieve a net income of close to $838.8 million during the same time frame. The substantial increase in revenue reflects the ongoing integration of fresh retail locations and strong consumer demand for high-performance athletic gear.

    As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is approximately 1.5x, indicating the business's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets that can be quickly converted to cash. The debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.4x, which compares total debt to shareholders' equity. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $400.2 million, providing the manufacturer with capital to reinvest in its growing store base.

    Etsy operates a unique marketplace model focused on creative, personalized items that are often difficult to find in significant-box retail stores. The platform connects roughly 5.6 million active sellers with about 86.5 million buyers globally, creating a vibrant ecosystem for independent entrepreneurs. Most of these sellers are small-scale businesses run by one person working from home, helping the manufacturer maintain an asset-light profile while serving a massive global audience.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $2.9 billion, representing a growth of roughly 2.1% compared to the prior twelve months. Net income for this period was close to $987.5 million, reflecting the efficiency of its marketplace-driven business model. While revenue growth has been modest, the tech giant continues to maintain significant profitability by providing essential infrastructure for millions of creative entrepreneurs to sell their goods.

    Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately -2.8x, indicating that total liabilities exceed shareholders' equity. The current ratio, which measures short-term liquidity, is approximately 1.4x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $638.8 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 35.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, as SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow.

    DICK'S Sporting Goods faces significant risks due to its heavy reliance on its primary vendor, which supplies nearly a third of its inventory. Macroeconomic conditions, such as inflation, can also hurt discretionary spending on athletic gear, especially during periods of economic uncertainty. The tech giant is currently working through the integration of the Foot Locker business and must navigate potential legal challenges related to inventory management and securities disclosures.

    According to recent reports, etsy faces intense competition from massive e-commerce rivals like Amazon (AMZN +1.69%)and specialized platforms such as eBay (EBAY -0.57%). Changes to search engine algorithms, particularly those from Alphabet, could significantly reduce the traffic flowing to its independent sellers. Additionally, the company must manage the evolving regulatory landscape concerning artificial intelligence, data privacy, and digital services taxes across its global markets.

    Recent findings suggest that DICK'S Sporting Goods appears to be the more conservatively valued option based on its lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio. The Forward P/E measures a stock's price relative to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio compares the market cap to sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    Sources indicate that when comparing Dick's and Etsy, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

    In a recent development, firstly, we should consider revenue growth. Since 2021, Dick's has generated average year-over-year revenue growth of 22%. Etsy, by contrast, has delivered average revenue growth of just 2%. That gives Dick's an edge in this category.

    Recent findings suggest that another factor to consider is each organization's profitability. Here, Etsy shows its strength. The company's operating margin now stands at 18.1%. That's well above Dick's, whose operating margin has fallen in recent quarters to 6.4%.

    It has been revealed that finally, there's valuation. Since both companies have been consistently profitable, we can examine their respective price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. Dick's P/E multiple is 15x, while Etsy's is only 10x.

    It has been revealed that to sum up, investors may want to consider both of these consumer stocks. However, in my opinion, Etsy comes out on top in this head-to-head matchup. Its combination of higher profitability and lower valuation makes it more appealing than Dick's, despite that tech giant's faster revenue growth.

    Il giudizio riguarda chi è rimasto a Roma durante la sosta; Agostinelli racconta anche di aver visto Frattesi sorridente.

    It has been revealed that la Lazio non ha staccato la spina durante la sosta: è questo l’aspetto che ha più colpito il protagonista dell’intervento riportato da Radiosei e che gli dà sicurezza per il futuro. A suo giudizio, i giocatori rimasti a Roma hanno mostrato di voler restare concentrati e di meritare spazio. Nel suo intervento ha parlato anche degli infortuni, di Frattesi e della sua conoscenza con Kurt Baldacchino.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    L’intervento si apre con una precisazione: «Premesso che la mia conoscenza con Kurt (Baldacchino, ndr) risale a tre anni fa.».

    Lui è il presidente del ‘Lazio club Malta’ e appunto tre anni fa mi premiò quando allenavo l’altra squadra di Malta (il Gudja United Club). Quest’anno si divide tra la mia squadra, il Mġarr United, e le giovanili. Sapevo di questa cosa e pensavo si potesse risolvere. Quando siamo arrivati, io sono andato a casa mia a Roma e con la squadra e ci siamo rivisti direttamente a Formello, incontro Kurt, bravo ragazzo e tifosissimo della Lazio, e mi dice che era rimasto fuori. Eravamo però a ridosso della gara, quindi ho raggiunto la squadra. Speravo la situazione si potesse risolvere poi invece non è andata così e mi è molto dispiaciuto perché pensavo potesse essere un ‘giorno di festa’. Ad ogni modo è un ragazzo splendido, ognuno può esprimere le sue idee non gli darei ‘la croce addosso’. Probabilmente il fatto si poteva risolvere in maniera serena.

    Industry observers note that gli infortuni della Lazio? Avendo degli staff molto numerosi ci sono confronti continui. Oggi lo staff è molto importante. Frattesi l’ho visto sorridente. Per me un giocatore può fare mille cose atletiche ma lo giudico ‘guarito’ se fa una partita, anche solo di 15′ perché non sei frenato durante la partitella. Questo però non significa che non ci saranno rischi in gara.

    Di questa Lazio l’aspetto che mi ha impressionato, e che mi dà sicurezza per il futuro, è che non hanno staccato la spina. Questo non è importante, di più. Significa che chi era a Roma durante la sosta ha voluto dimostrare di stare sul pezzo, di meritare spazio”.

    #38989. Tech Report: Ray Dalio indicates Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    Tech Report: Ray Dalio indicates Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • Sources indicate that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    Sources indicate that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio noted. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Bessent remarked in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    To solve this, Dalio mentioned the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    Recent findings suggest that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he noted.

    It has been revealed that dalio stated it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Dalio stated the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder remarked.

    In a recent development, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday.
    • The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.
    • The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

    Industry observers note that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

    MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE.

    Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

    Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

    Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

    AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    According to recent reports, chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:.

    He is among the newly introduced breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

    It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

    Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the upcoming season.

    AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

    Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2.

    Industry observers note that the final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

    What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj.

    Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

    A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

    Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

    Industry observers note that chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

    It has been revealed that chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

    Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

    Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

    Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

    Time for the second half water break.

    Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and promptly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

    Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

    AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

    AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

    Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

    Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

    Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

    According to recent reports, chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

    Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

    Sources indicate that AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their fresh record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

    Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

    Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2.

    The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

    90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

    Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

    Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

    Sources indicate that the first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

    Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

    In a recent development, then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

    Sources indicate that the space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

    Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

    We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

    Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

    Industry observers note that that is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

    Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

    A significant, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

    In a recent development, chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

    Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

    Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

    Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

    Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

    Industry observers note that we are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

    It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

    The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

    Sources indicate that the trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, Undisclosed.

    OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, Loan.

    Recent findings suggest that in Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

    In a recent development, our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708.

    July 28- Western Sydney Wanderers 4 Chelsea 6August 1- Chelsea 1 Tottenham 2August 5- Chelsea 0 Juventus 1Today- Chelsea vs AC MilanAugust 9- Johor Darul Ta’z vs ChelseaAugust 15- Chelsea vs Real Sociedad.

    Current Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo has been catching up with former Chelsea men Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who starts for AC Milan today, and Fikayo Tomori.

    The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8.

    The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have fresh managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    Sources indicate that “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso noted in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    Sources indicate that it has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    Sources indicate that AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Il difensore danese piace all'Inter su indicazione di Chivu, ma il club biancoceleste non fa sconti e fissa il prezzo a 40 milioni.
    • Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, l'Inter avrebbe messo nel mirino Oliver Provstgaard, giovane difensore rivelazione della Lazio, su esplicita richiesta di Cristian Chivu per rinforzare la retroguardia.
    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Il difensore danese piace all'Inter su indicazione di Chivu, ma il club biancoceleste non fa sconti e fissa il prezzo a 40 milioni.

    Secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, l'Inter avrebbe messo nel mirino Oliver Provstgaard, giovane difensore rivelazione della Lazio, su esplicita richiesta di Cristian Chivu per rinforzare la retroguardia. Per il club biancoceleste, tuttavia, il centrale rappresenta ormai un punto fermo: grazie al lavoro svolto sotto la guida di Gennaro Gattuso, il giocatore ha compiuto un netto salto di qualità sfornendo in questa stagione prove di grande solidità.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    Il centrale danese ha conquistato gli osservatori nerazzurri grazie a prestazioni di altissimo livello, convincendo la dirigenza milanese a considerarlo il profilo ideale per la difesa. Chivu vede in lui la soluzione perfetta per un reparto che necessita di interventi mirati in ottica presente e futura.

    Tuttavia, l'operazione si prospetta complessa: Claudio Lotito non ha intenzione di svendere il danese  e per privarsi del difensore a gennaio chiederebbe una cifra vicina ai 40 milioni di euro. Per questo motivo, l'Inter continua a monitorare anche alternative come Mario Hermoso, in scadenza con la Roma nel giugno 2027, pronto a inserirsi in caso di mancato accordo per il rinnovo.
